answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: After a tax lien has been held long enough, the lawful holder of the certificate of purchase may apply for a treasurer's deed; the county treasurer then holds a public auction, and the winning bidder receives a certificate of option for a treasurer's deed.
answers.quote: AFTER AUGUST 1 OF THE THIRD CALENDAR YEAR FOLLOWING THE DATE OF A TAX LIEN SALE, A LAWFUL HOLDER MAY APPLY FOR A TREASURER'S DEED FOR THE PROPERTY DESCRIBED IN THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ... "CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED" MEANS A CERTIFICATE ISSUED BY A TREASURER TO THE SUCCESSFUL PURCHASER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: The first public auction must be scheduled no less than thirty and no more than sixty calendar days after the treasurer mails the notice of public auction.
answers.quote: THE INITIAL PUBLIC AUCTION HELD PURSUANT TO THIS ARTICLE 11.5 MUST BE SCHEDULED FOR NO LESS THAN THIRTY CALENDAR DAYS NOR MORE THAN SIXTY CALENDAR DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF MAILING THE NOTICE OF PUBLIC AUCTION.

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: The treasurer holds the public auction at a courthouse or at a building housing the county clerk and recorder or the treasurer, as named in the notice; it may also be held on the internet or another electronic medium.
answers.quote: THE TREASURER SHALL CONDUCT THE PUBLIC AUCTION AT ANY DOOR OR ENTRANCE TO, OR IN ANY ROOM IN ANY BUILDING TEMPORARILY OR PERMANENTLY USED AS, A COURTHOUSE OR AT OR WITHIN ANY BUILDING WHERE THE OFFICE OF THE COUNTY CLERK AND RECORDER OR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER IS LOCATED, WHICH PLACE MUST BE SPECIFICALLY DESIGNATED IN THE NOTICE OF PUBLIC AUCTION; EXCEPT THAT A PUBLIC AUCTION MAY ALSO BE CONDUCTED BY MEANS OF THE INTERNET OR OTHER ELECTRONIC MEDIUM.

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: The statutory notice of public auction tells interested bidders that they must register and gives the treasurer's website or office phone number for more information.
answers.quote: INTERESTED BIDDERS MUST REGISTER. MORE INFORMATION AT (WEBSITE OR TREASURER'S OFFICE PHONE NUMBER).

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: The statute sets no deposit for third-party bidders; each treasurer's posted bidding rules do. SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: The treasurer may require the lawful holder who applies for a treasurer's deed to deposit up to one thousand dollars plus the permitted fees when the application is accepted, applied against the treasurer's fees and costs. Bidding rules for the public auction are posted on the treasurer's website or the auction medium at least fourteen calendar days before the auction.
answers.quote: THE TREASURER MAY REQUIRE THE LAWFUL HOLDER TO MAKE A DEPOSIT OF UP TO ONE THOUSAND DOLLARS PLUS THE AMOUNT OF FEES PERMITTED PURSUANT TO SECTION 30-1-102 (1.7), AT THE TIME THE APPLICATION FOR TREASURER'S DEED IS ACCEPTED, TO BE APPLIED AGAINST THE FEES AND COSTS OF THE TREASURER IN PROCEEDING PURSUANT TO THIS ARTICLE 11.5. ... BIDDING RULES FOR THE PUBLIC AUCTION WILL BE POSTED ON THE TREASURER'S WEBSITE OR THE ELECTRONIC MEDIUM USED TO CONDUCT THE AUCTION AT LEAST FOURTEEN CALENDAR DAYS BEFORE THE DATE OF THE PUBLIC AUCTION.

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted. A page header falls inside subsection (6) in the PDF, so that sentence is quoted in two pieces.
answers.answer: The lawful holder must bid no less than the total debt as determined by the treasurer; the bid form sets out all money due to the lawful holder, including the treasurer's fees and costs.
answers.quote: MUST SET FORTH ALL MONEY DUE AND OWING TO THE LAWFUL HOLDER, INCLUDING ALL TREASURER FEES AND COSTS ... A LAWFUL HOLDER MUST BID NO LESS THAN THE AMOUNT OF THE TOTAL DEBT, ... AS DETERMINED BY THE TREASURER, FOR THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE BEING SOLD.

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: Payment of the amount bid must reach the treasurer by the date and time of the auction, or at another time on the auction day that the treasurer sets in writing, in the form the treasurer specifies. If the highest bidder does not pay in full, the next highest bidder who pays in time is the successful bidder.
answers.quote: THE PAYMENT OF ANY AMOUNT BID AT AN AUCTION MUST BE RECEIVED BY A TREASURER NO LATER THAN THE DATE AND TIME OF THE AUCTION, OR AT AN ALTERNATIVE TIME AFTER THE AUCTION AND ON THE DAY OF THE AUCTION, AS SPECIFIED IN WRITING BY THE TREASURER. A BID PAYMENT MUST BE MADE IN THE FORM SPECIFIED BY THE TREASURER.

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: If the property is sold to a third-party bidder, or to the lawful holder bidding competitively, the treasurer may collect up to three hundred dollars from the successful bidder for processing the public auction.
answers.quote: IF A PROPERTY IS SOLD TO A THIRD-PARTY BIDDER OR A LAWFUL HOLDER AS A COMPETITIVE BIDDER, A TREASURER MAY COLLECT UP TO THREE HUNDRED DOLLARS FROM THE SUCCESSFUL BIDDER FOR PERFORMING ACTIONS RELATED TO PROCESSING THE PUBLIC AUCTION

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: When the repurchase period ends, title vests in the holder of the certificate of option, and the treasurer executes and records a treasurer's deed confirming the transfer.
answers.quote: UPON THE EXPIRATION OF THE REPURCHASE PERIOD ... TITLE TO THE PROPERTY VESTS IN THE HOLDER OF THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... THE TREASURER SHALL EXECUTE AND RECORD A TREASURER'S DEED PURSUANT TO SECTION 39-11.5-502 TO THE HOLDER OF THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... CONFIRMING THE TRANSFER OF TITLE TO THE PROPERTY.

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: The property owner may redeem before the auction by filing an intent to redeem no later than seven calendar days before the scheduled auction. After the auction, a lawful holder who did not win may repurchase the certificate of option by noon on the eighth business day after the auction.
answers.quote: A PROPERTY OWNER IS ENTITLED TO REDEEM A PROPERTY IF, NO LATER THAN SEVEN CALENDAR DAYS PRIOR TO THE CURRENTLY SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, THE PROPERTY OWNER FILES AN INTENT TO REDEEM ... NO LATER THAN NOON ON THE EIGHTH BUSINESS DAY FOLLOWING THE PUBLIC AUCTION, THE LAWFUL HOLDER MAY REPURCHASE THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: Subject to junior lienors' overbid claims, title is free and clear of liens and encumbrances junior to the certificate of purchase. The treasurer's deed does not affect existing roads, rights-of-way, conservation easements, other easements or equitable servitudes.
answers.quote: THE TITLE IS FREE AND CLEAR OF ALL LIENS AND ENCUMBRANCES JUNIOR TO THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ... EXECUTION OF A TREASURER'S DEED PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION DOES NOT AFFECT THE EXISTENCE OF ANY PUBLIC OR PRIVATE ROADS, RIGHTS-OF-WAY, CONSERVATION EASEMENTS, OTHER EASEMENTS, OR EQUITABLE SERVITUDES

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: If no valid bids are received at the public auction, the lawful holder who does not withdraw the application becomes the purchaser.
answers.quote: "PURCHASER" MEANS A PERSON TO WHOM THE TREASURER AWARDS THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED AS THE WINNING BIDDER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION WHO TIMELY SUBMITS PROPER FUNDS, OR, IF NO VALID BIDS ARE RECEIVED AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION, THE LAWFUL HOLDER WHO DOES NOT FILE A WITHDRAWAL OF THE APPLICATION

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: Once the claim period ends, remaining overbid is paid in order of recording priority to junior lienors who filed a claim, up to their unpaid lien plus fees and costs. Any overbid money left after that is paid to the property owner.
answers.quote: ANY REMAINING OVERBID MUST BE PAID IN ORDER OF RECORDING PRIORITY TO JUNIOR LIENORS ... AFTER PAYMENT TO ALL JUNIOR LIENORS ENTITLED TO RECEIVE A PORTION OF THE OVERBID PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION ... ANY REMAINING OVERBID MONEY MUST BE PAID TO THE PROPERTY OWNER

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: No statewide statutory due-diligence instruction to buyers was found; county treasurers' pages carry 'buyer beware' warnings (see county rows).
answers.where_to_look: See Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144).

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.summary: County-held tax lien certificates offered for assignment by the treasurer; the lien, not the land.

answers.source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
answers.note: SB 26-144 amended 39-11-117 (wording only); quoted words are unchanged.
answers.answer: The treasurer prepares a certificate of purchase for the purchaser of a tax lien on real property sold for delinquent taxes; it describes the property and states the rate of interest and the total taxes, delinquent interest and fees.
answers.quote: The treasurer shall prepare, sign, and retain for safekeeping or deliver to the purchaser of a tax lien on any real property sold for the payment of delinquent taxes a certificate of purchase describing the property on which the taxes and fees were paid by the purchaser, as the same was described in the record of sales, and also stating the rate of interest and the total amount of all taxes, delinquent interest, and fees

answers.source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
answers.note: SB 26-144 amended 39-11-115(1): 'shall' became 'MUST' in the last sentence; the rule is otherwise unchanged.
answers.answer: Tax liens are sold to the bidders who pay the taxes, delinquent interest and fees, or who pay the largest amount above them (a premium); the excess goes to the county general fund.
answers.quote: sold to the persons who pay therefor the taxes, delinquent interest, and fees then due thereon or who further pay the largest amount in excess of said taxes, delinquent interest, and fees. The excess amount shall be credited to the county general fund.

answers.source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
answers.note: Read from the 2024 C.R.S. title 39 printout (the newest posted); SB 26-144 (2026) does not amend this section.
answers.answer: Redemption interest is nine percentage points above the discount rate a commercial bank pays the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, rounded to the nearest full percent.
answers.quote: The annual rate of redemption interest shall be nine percentage points above the discount rate, which discount rate shall be the rate of interest a commercial bank pays to the federal reserve bank of Kansas City using a government bond or other eligible paper as security, and shall be rounded to the nearest full percent.

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: The earlier quote mixed 39-12-103(3) (2024 C.R.S. printout: redemption at any time before a treasurer's deed is executed; three years before a holder may apply) with this session law; this row quotes the session law only. SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: Under the treasurer's deed auction process, the owner must file an intent to redeem no later than seven calendar days before the scheduled public auction; the treasurer's redemption statement is effective for ten business days or until noon the day before the auction, whichever is first, and the owner may redeem at any time before it expires.
answers.quote: A PROPERTY OWNER IS ENTITLED TO REDEEM A PROPERTY IF, NO LATER THAN SEVEN CALENDAR DAYS PRIOR TO THE CURRENTLY SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, THE PROPERTY OWNER FILES AN INTENT TO REDEEM THE PROPERTY WITH THE TREASURER. ... A REDEMPTION STATEMENT IS EFFECTIVE FOR TEN BUSINESS DAYS OR UNTIL NOON THE DAY BEFORE THE CURRENTLY SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, WHICHEVER OCCURS FIRST. ... A PROPERTY OWNER MAY REDEEM A PROPERTY AT ANY TIME BEFORE THE EXPIRATION OF A REDEMPTION STATEMENT BY PAYING THE TREASURER

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: After August 1 of the third calendar year after the tax lien sale, the lawful holder may apply for a treasurer's deed. The property then goes to a public auction; if the holder is not the winning bidder, the holder may repurchase the certificate of option within the repurchase period.
answers.quote: AFTER AUGUST 1 OF THE THIRD CALENDAR YEAR FOLLOWING THE DATE OF A TAX LIEN SALE, A LAWFUL HOLDER MAY APPLY FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... A LAWFUL HOLDER IS ENTITLED TO REPURCHASE A CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED IF THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENTS ARE MET TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE TREASURER: (a) THE LAWFUL HOLDER WAS NOT THE SUCCESSFUL PURCHASER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: Quoted as the session law prints: lower-case words ('shall', 'fifteen') are the struck prior text and capitals ('MAY', 'SEVEN') the enacted text; the section also keeps the rule from applying to certificates held by the county. SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: As amended, a lien created by a certificate of purchase may not remain a lien longer than seven years after its original issuance. A certificate issued before January 1, 2026 may remain a lien for fifteen years after issuance.
answers.quote: No lien upon real property created by a tax certificate or a certificate of purchase issued by a treasurer on account of any delinquent property taxes or any special assessment of any kind or nature shall MAY remain a lien thereon for a period longer than fifteen SEVEN years after the original issuance thereof ... NOTWITHSTANDING ANY OTHER PROVISION OF THIS SECTION, A LIEN ON PROPERTY CREATED BY A TAX LIEN SALE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 1, 2026, MAY REMAIN A LIEN FOR A PERIOD OF FIFTEEN YEARS AFTER THE DATE OF ISSUANCE.

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: Session-law text: lower-case words struck through ('four', 'land') are deleted; capitals are new. Quoted exactly as printed.
answers.answer: Under the amended fee schedule the county treasurer charges FIVE dollars for each certificate of purchase delivered from a tax lien sale, and FIVE dollars for assigning a county-held certificate to a person who wants to buy it.
answers.quote: (i) For each certificate of purchase delivered, four FROM A TAX LIEN SALE, FIVE ... (l) For the assignment of a certificate of purchase, made to the county, city, town, or city and county at any tax sale, to a person desiring to purchase land PROPERTY covered by such certificate, four FIVE dollars

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: Quoted as the session law prints 39-11-148(2): lower-case words are the struck prior text and capitals the enacted text. SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
answers.answer: No treasurer's deed may issue after a public auction on a certificate of purchase that has ceased to be a lien under the limitation section. An injunction or bankruptcy petition automatically stays the treasurer from conducting the public auction; the treasurer announces that fact and takes no action on the scheduled date.
answers.quote: No treasurer's deed shall MAY issue on AFTER PUBLIC AUCTION IN CONNECTION WITH any tax LIEN sale evidenced by tax certificate or certificate of purchase where such tax certificate or THE certificate of purchase has ceased to be a lien pursuant to the provisions of this section ... BEFORE ANY INJUNCTION OR BANKRUPTCY PETITION IS FILED WHICH AUTOMATICALLY STAYS THE TREASURER FROM CONDUCTING THE PUBLIC AUCTION, THE TREASURER SHALL ANNOUNCE, POST, OR PROVIDE NOTICE OF THAT FACT ON THE THEN-SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, TAKE NO ACTION AT THE THEN-SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION

answers.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
answers.note: Session-law text: lower-case struck words are deleted, capitals are new; quoted exactly as printed.
answers.answer: A county holding certificates of purchase from tax lien sales may assign, sell or transfer them in the manner, at the times and on the terms its board of county commissioners sets by resolution.
answers.quote: Any county in this state having in its possession or under its control certificates of purchase resulting from the sale of a tax lien on land PROPERTY for the nonpayment of general taxes may assign, sell, or transfer such THOSE certificates OF PURCHASE in such manner, at such times, and on such terms as may be determined by resolution of the board of county commissioners

answers.answer: The Douglas County Treasurer's office handles the tax lien sale, county-held liens and treasurer's deeds: phone 303-660-7455, general information 303-660-7400.

answers.note: Same page: 2026 interest is 13%; payment for winning bids is by ACH from the bank account given at registration.
answers.answer: Douglas County's 2026 internet tax lien sale is held November 5, 2026 through zeusauction.com. It is a premium auction: the minimum starting bid is the delinquent taxes, interest, advertising and fees, and bidders may bid above it; premiums are never returned and draw no interest.

answers.source_title: Request for Assignment of County-Held Tax Lien (Douglas County Treasurer)
answers.answer: Any tax lien purchase is at the purchaser's own risk. The county names properties in bankruptcy, under RTC, FDIC or DEA control, with special improvement assessments, or with environmental conditions, and says such purchases may result in a loss of investment and/or interest.
answers.quote: Any purchase of a tax lien is done at the purchaser’s own risk. ... Particular attention should be given to those properties in bankruptcy; under the control of the Resolution Trust Corporation (RTC), the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), or the Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA); any properties involving a special improvement assessment ... and any property with environmental conditions that may prove undesirable/detrimental. The purchase of a tax lien on these properties may result in a loss of investment and/or interest.

answers.source_title: Request for Assignment of County-Held Tax Lien (Douglas County Treasurer)
answers.answer: County-held tax liens are requested with the treasurer's Request for Assignment of County-Held Tax Lien form; all county-held liens on the parcel listed must be redeemed, and the buyer signs an acknowledgment of the risk involved.
answers.quote: REQUEST FOR ASSIGNMENT OF COUNTY-HELD TAX LIEN ... All County held liens on the parcel listed below MUST be redeemed ... My signature below acknowledges that I understand and except the element of risk involved in purchasing tax lien(s) as stated in the disclaimer.

answers.source_title: Request for Assignment of County-Held Tax Lien (Douglas County Treasurer)
answers.answer: The purchaser assumes the responsibility of determining the status of any property offered at the tax lien sale.
answers.quote: The purchaser assumes the responsibility of determining the status of any property offered at tax lien sale.

AUCTIONS.summary: A clerk's tax deed sale: the property itself is sold to the highest bidder at a scheduled public auction.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
answers.answer: Property on which a tax deed application has been filed is sold at public auction to the highest bidder by the clerk of the circuit court of the county where the property is located.
answers.quote: Real property advertised for sale to the highest bidder as a result of an application filed under s. 197.502 shall be sold at public auction by the clerk of the circuit court, or his or her deputy, of the county where the property is located

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: Re-scoped 2026-11-02 to the cited page only: the notice rule (publication once a week for four consecutive weeks; no sale until 30 days after the first publication) is in F.S. 197.512(1), https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0197/Sections/0197.512.html
answers.answer: The clerk sells the property at public auction on the date, at the time and at the location set out in the published notice, which must be during the clerk's regular office hours.
answers.quote: on the date, at the time, and at the location as set forth in the published notice, which must be during the regular hours the clerk's office is open

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
answers.answer: A clerk may hold electronic tax deed sales instead of public outcry, with electronic proxy bidding allowed. The clerk must provide public computer terminals for the electronic sale at a designated location.
answers.quote: A clerk may conduct electronic tax deed sales in lieu of public outcry. The clerk must comply with the procedures provided in this chapter, except that electronic proxy bidding shall be allowed ... The clerk shall provide access to the electronic sale by computer terminals open to the public at a designated location.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
answers.answer: The statute lets the clerk require bidders to show their willingness and ability to post the deposit, and at an electronic sale to advance enough funds to pay the deposit. Each county's own registration steps are in its county rows.
answers.quote: the clerk may require bidders to show their willingness and ability to post the deposit ... electronic proxy bidding shall be allowed and the clerk may require bidders to advance sufficient funds to pay the deposit required by subsection (2).

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
answers.answer: The high bidder must post a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, at the time of the sale; it is applied to the price at full payment.
answers.quote: The high bidder shall post with the clerk a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, at the time of the sale, to be applied to the sale price at the time of full payment.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: Re-read 2026-10-29; same provision as the VERIFIED opening_bid rule in data/state_rules.csv. F.S. 197.502(6)(b) sets the opening bid on an individual's certificate.
answers.answer: On county-held certificates on nonhomestead property, the opening bid is the value of all outstanding certificates plus omitted years' taxes, delinquent taxes, current taxes if due, interest, and all costs and fees paid by the county. On property assessed as homestead on the latest roll it also includes one-half of the latest assessed value.
answers.quote: On county-held certificates on nonhomestead property shall be the sum of the value of all outstanding certificates against the property, plus omitted years' taxes, delinquent taxes, current taxes, if due, interest, and all costs and fees paid by the county. ... an amount equal to one-half of the latest assessed value of the homestead.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
answers.answer: Full payment of the final bid, documentary stamp tax and recording fees is due within 24 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays. If it is not made, the clerk cancels all bids, readvertises the sale and pays the sale costs from the deposit.
answers.quote: If full payment of the final bid and of documentary stamp tax and recording fees is not made within 24 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays, the clerk shall cancel all bids, readvertise the sale as provided in this section, and pay all costs of the sale from the deposit.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: Quote re-copied 2026-11-02: the statute page prints the cross-reference as 's. 28.24 (11)' with a space.
answers.answer: On top of the final bid, the buyer pays the documentary stamp tax and recording fees. At an electronic sale, the winning bidder's advance deposit is subject to the fee under s. 28.24 (11).
answers.quote: full payment of the final bid and of documentary stamp tax and recording fees ... The portion of an advance deposit from a winning bidder required by subsection (2) shall, upon acceptance of the winning bid, be subject to the fee under s. 28.24 (11).

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.552 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: Immediate possession: F.S. 197.562 ('shall be entitled to the immediate possession of the lands described in the deed').
answers.answer: The buyer receives a tax deed issued in the name of the county and signed by the clerk. The deed is prima facie evidence that all proceedings were regular, and the grantee is entitled to immediate possession.
answers.quote: All tax deeds shall be issued in the name of a county and shall be signed by the clerk of the county. ... All deeds issued pursuant to this section shall be prima facie evidence of the regularity of all proceedings from the valuation of the lands to the issuance of the deed, inclusive.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.472 (Online Sunshine)
answers.answer: A certificate can be redeemed at any time before a tax deed is issued, unless full payment for the tax deed, including documentary stamps and recording fees, has been made to the clerk.
answers.quote: A person may redeem a tax certificate at any time after the certificate is issued and before a tax deed is issued unless full payment for a tax deed is made to the clerk of the court, including documentary stamps and recording fees.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.552 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: Quote split 2026-11-02 at the cross-reference, which the statute page prints as 's. 197.582 ,' with a space. F.S. 197.573 (https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0197/Sections/0197.573.html) separately keeps recorded use restrictions and covenants running with the land enforceable after a tax deed, while forfeitures, rights of reentry and reverter rights are destroyed.
answers.answer: Except as the chapter provides, no right, interest, restriction or covenant survives the tax deed, but a lien of record held by a municipal or county governmental unit, special district or community development district that is not satisfied from the sale proceeds survives.
answers.quote: Except as specifically provided in this chapter, no right, interest, restriction, or other covenant shall survive the issuance of a tax deed, except that a lien of record held by a municipal or county governmental unit, special district, or community development district, when such lien is not satisfied as of the disbursement of proceeds of sale under the provisions of s. 197.582 ... shall survive the issuance of a tax deed.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.552 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: The statute says nothing about title insurance or a quiet-title action; several clerks' pages state that a tax deed does not warrant or guarantee clear and marketable title (see the county rows).
answers.answer: Under s. 197.552 a tax deed is prima facie evidence of the regularity of all proceedings from the valuation of the lands to the issuance of the deed.
answers.quote: All deeds issued pursuant to this section shall be prima facie evidence of the regularity of all proceedings from the valuation of the lands to the issuance of the deed, inclusive.

answers.source_title: Florida Statutes 197.562 - Grantee of tax deed entitled to immediate possession
answers.answer: The grantee of a tax deed is entitled to immediate possession of the land. If a demand for possession is refused, the purchaser may apply to the circuit court for a writ of assistance upon 5 days' notice, and if the court finds for the applicant it orders the sheriff to put the grantee in possession.
answers.quote: Any person, firm, corporation, or county that is the grantee of any tax deed under this law shall be entitled to the immediate possession of the lands described in the deed. If a demand for possession is refused, the purchaser may apply to the circuit court for a writ of assistance upon 5 days’ notice directed to the person refusing to deliver possession. ... If the court finds for the applicant, an order shall be issued by the court directing the sheriff to put the grantee in possession of the lands.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: F.S. 197.542(1): 'If there are no higher bids, the property shall be struck off and sold to the certificateholder'.
answers.answer: If there are no higher bids the property is struck off to the certificateholder. If there are no bidders and the certificateholder does not pay resale costs or the amounts due for the deed within 30 days after the sale, the clerk puts the land on the list of lands available for taxes.
answers.quote: On county-held or individually held certificates for which there are no bidders at the public sale and for which the certificateholder fails to timely pay costs of resale or fails to pay the amounts due for issuance of a tax deed within 30 days after the sale, the clerk shall enter the land on a list entitled "lands available for taxes"

answers.source_title: Florida Statutes 197.582 - Disbursement of proceeds of sale
answers.answer: If the property sells for more than the certificateholder's statutory bid, the clerk pays the surplus first to governmental units for liens of record they hold, then keeps any balance for the benefit of persons described in s. 197.522(1)(a). A claimant has 120 days from the date of the notice to file a written claim with the clerk for the surplus proceeds.
answers.quote: If the property is purchased for an amount in excess of the statutory bid of the certificateholder, the surplus must be paid over and disbursed by the clerk ... The clerk shall distribute the surplus to the governmental units for the payment of any lien of record held by a governmental unit against the property ... If there remains a balance of undistributed funds, the balance must be retained by the clerk for the benefit of persons described in s. 197.522 (1)(a) ... has 120 days from the date of the notice to file a written claim with the clerk for the surplus proceeds.

answers.note: Chapter 197 contains no buyer due-diligence checklist; county clerks publish their own 'as is' / buyer-beware notices.

AVAILABLE.summary: Property that failed to sell at a tax deed sale, purchasable from the clerk without an auction (Lands Available for Taxes).

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
answers.answer: These are properties offered at a tax deed sale that drew no bidders, where the certificateholder did not pay resale costs or the amounts due for the deed within 30 days. The clerk enters them on the list of lands available for taxes and notifies the county commission.
answers.quote: On county-held or individually held certificates for which there are no bidders at the public sale and for which the certificateholder fails to timely pay costs of resale or fails to pay the amounts due for issuance of a tax deed within 30 days after the sale, the clerk shall enter the land on a list entitled "lands available for taxes" and shall immediately notify the county commission that the property is available.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: Re-read 2026-10-29; same provision as the VERIFIED available_after_sale rule in data/state_rules.csv.
answers.answer: For the first 90 days only the county may buy the land (or waive its right). After that, any person may purchase the property from the clerk, without further notice or advertising, for the opening bid.
answers.quote: During the first 90 days after the property is placed on the list, the county may purchase the land for the opening bid or may waive its rights to purchase the property. Thereafter, any person, the county, or any other governmental unit may purchase the property from the clerk, without further notice or advertising, for the opening bid

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: FIXED 2026-11-02 (capture PARTIAL). Quote spacing follows the page text as the capture extracts it (a space before the punctuation that follows a linked section number).
answers.answer: The price is the opening bid. Interest on the opening bid keeps accruing through the month of sale, and each year's taxes that would have been due are treated as omitted years and added to the required minimum bid.
answers.quote: for the opening bid ... Interest on the opening bid continues to accrue through the month of sale as prescribed by s. 197.542 . (8) Taxes may not be extended against parcels listed as lands available for taxes, but in each year the taxes that would have been due shall be treated as omitted years and added to the required minimum bid.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: FIXED 2026-11-02 (capture NOT_FOUND). Quote spacing follows the page text as the capture extracts it (a space before the punctuation that follows a linked section number). The documentary stamp / recording-fee language of F.S. 197.542(1) is written for the certificateholder after a no-bid sale, not for a list purchaser.
answers.answer: The statute adds accrued interest on the opening bid through the month of sale and the omitted years' taxes to the required minimum bid. County clerks list their own additional charges in the county rows.
answers.quote: Interest on the opening bid continues to accrue through the month of sale as prescribed by s. 197.542 . (8) Taxes may not be extended against parcels listed as lands available for taxes, but in each year the taxes that would have been due shall be treated as omitted years and added to the required minimum bid.

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.summary: A tax certificate: a lien on the property for unpaid taxes, bought by assignment from the county. It is not ownership of the land.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.102 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: FIXED 2026-11-02 (capture NOT_FOUND). Quote spacing follows the page text as the capture extracts it (a space before the punctuation that follows a linked section number). Sale by the tax collector: F.S. 197.432(1).
answers.answer: A tax certificate is a paper or electronic legal document representing unpaid delinquent real property taxes, non-ad valorem assessments, interest and related costs and charges, issued against a specific parcel of real property and becoming a first lien on it, superior to all other liens except as provided by s. 197.573(2).
answers.quote: “Tax certificate” means a paper or electronic legal document, representing unpaid delinquent real property taxes, non-ad valorem assessments, including special assessments, interest, and related costs and charges, issued in accordance with this chapter against a specific parcel of real property and becoming a first lien thereon, superior to all other liens, except as provided by s. 197.573 (2).

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.432 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: Same section: 'If a certificate is not purchased, the certificate shall be struck to the county at the maximum rate of interest allowed by this chapter'; (7) 'The tax collector may require payment of a reasonable deposit'.
answers.answer: Each certificate goes to the bidder who will pay the taxes, interest, costs and charges and demand the lowest interest rate, up to the maximum. Bids are in quarter-percent steps; unsold certificates are struck to the county at the maximum rate. The tax collector may require a deposit and may sell electronically with proxy bidding.
answers.quote: Each certificate shall be awarded to the person who will pay the taxes, interest, costs, and charges and will demand the lowest rate of interest, not in excess of the maximum rate of interest allowed by this chapter. The tax collector shall accept bids in even increments and in fractional interest rate bids of one-quarter of 1 percent only.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.172 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: FIXED 2026-11-02 (capture PARTIAL): the former quote mixed in two passages from F.S. 197.472(2) (the mandatory 5 percent minimum charge), which are not on the 197.172 page; the capture matches one page only. The 5 percent minimum is at https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0197/Sections/0197.472.html.
answers.answer: The maximum rate of interest on a tax certificate is 18 percent per year, and interest is calculated from the first day of each month.
answers.quote: The maximum rate of interest on a tax certificate is 18 percent per year. ... Interest shall be calculated from the first day of each month.

answers.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.472 (Online Sunshine)
answers.note: Resolves the UNRESOLVED redemption row in data/state_rules.csv.
answers.answer: A certificate may be redeemed at any time after it is issued and before a tax deed is issued, unless full payment for the tax deed, including documentary stamps and recording fees, has been made to the clerk. The redeemer pays the tax collector the face amount plus all interest, costs and charges.

answers.source_title: Tax Certificate Sale Basics (Alachua County Tax Collector)
answers.answer: The sale is held electronically over the internet on or shortly before June 1 each year; the bidder accepting the lowest interest rate wins and pays the delinquent taxes, late-payment penalties, costs of the sale, and advertising charges.

answers.source_title: Tax Certificate Sale Basics (Alachua County Tax Collector)
answers.answer: Some parcels may be easements, landlocked property, alleyways, or other property of little or no value, and there are no guarantees certificates will be good investments. Certificates are canceled after seven years unless extended by actions such as bankruptcy, and can be canceled for statutory errors with 8 percent interest or the bid amount, whichever is lower.
answers.quote: Some of the parcels may be easements, landlocked property, alleyways, or other property that has little or no value. There are no guarantees that tax certificates will turn out to be good investments. By law, certificates are canceled after seven years unless extended by some administrative action such as bankruptcy. Certificates can be canceled due to certain statutory errors, in which case the bidder will receive 8 percent interest or the bid amount, whichever is lower.

answers.source_title: Tax Certificate Sale Basics (Alachua County Tax Collector)

Certificates can be transferred to another individual by paying a small fee to the Tax Collector.

answers.source_title: Calhoun County Tax Deed Sale Process
answers.office: Calhoun County Clerk of the Circuit Court & County Comptroller
answers.answer: Questions about the tax deed sale procedure go to the Calhoun County Clerk's office at 850-674-4545.
answers.quote: If you have additional questions concerning the procedure for tax deed sales, please refer to Florida Statutes Chapter 197 or contact the Clerk’s office at 850-674-4545 .

answers.source_title: Calhoun County Tax Deed Sale Process
answers.answer: Notices of pending tax deed sales are published in a newspaper with local circulation; sales begin at 10:00 a.m.
answers.quote: Notices of pending Tax Deed Sales are published in a newspaper with local circulation. ... Sales will be held beginning at 10:00 a.m. in the front lobby of the Calhoun County Courthouse

answers.source_title: Calhoun County Tax Deed Sale Process
answers.answer: Sales are held in person in the front lobby of the Calhoun County Courthouse at 20859 Central Ave. E., Blountstown, beginning at 10:00 a.m.
answers.quote: Sales will be held beginning at 10:00 a.m. in the front lobby of the Calhoun County Courthouse at 20859 Central Ave. E. Blountstown, FL, 32424.

answers.source_title: Calhoun County Tax Deed Sale Process
answers.answer: Anyone may bid on a property; there is no pre-registration required.
answers.quote: Anyone may bid on a property there is no pre-registration required.

answers.source_title: Calhoun County Tax Deed Sale Process
answers.answer: The successful high bidder must remit the total bid or a 5 % deposit of the total sale, with the balance paid within 24 hours of the sale.
answers.quote: Once a sale had been completed, the successful high bidder must remit to the Clerk the total bid or 5 % deposit down of the total sale with the balance being paid within 24 hours of the sale

answers.source_title: Calhoun County Tax Deed Sale Process
answers.answer: The balance is due within 24 hours of the sale, in cash or cashier's check payable to the Calhoun County Clerk's Office.
answers.quote: with the balance being paid within 24 hours of the sale ... Payment may be made in the form of cash or cashier’s check payable to the Calhoun County Clerk’s Office.

answers.source_title: Calhoun County Tax Deed Sale Process
answers.answer: The winning bidder also pays recording fees of $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for any additional pages, plus State Documentary Stamps of $0.70 per $100.00 of the bid.
answers.quote: as well as the recording fees of $10.00 for the first page, $8.50 for any additional pages and State Documentary Stamps of $0.70 per $100.00 of the bid.

answers.source_title: Calhoun County Tax Deed Sale Process
answers.answer: The Clerk's page tells bidders they must do their own research for each property, and that the Clerk's office assumes no responsibility for any encumbrances on any property offered for sale.
answers.quote: You must do your own research for each property! ... The Clerk’s office assumes no responsibility for any encumbrances on any property offered for sale.

answers.source_title: Clerk of Court - Tax Deed Services (Frequently Asked Questions)
answers.answer: You must have $200.00 or 5% of the winning bid, whichever is greater, on deposit with RealAuction for each tax deed where you are the highest bidder. Deposits can be made by cashier's check or money order at the Clerk's office, by ACH (usually 4-5 business days) or by wire (usually 24-48 hours).
answers.quote: You are also required to have $200.00 or 5% of the winning bid, whichever is greater, on deposit with RealAuction for each tax deed where you are the highest bidder. … ACH from your bank account to your RealAuction account, this process usually takes 4-5 business days. … Wire payments from your bank account to your RealAuction account, this process usually takes 24-48 hours.

answers.source_title: Clerk of Court - Tax Deed Services (General Information)
answers.answer: The bid amount, plus recording fees and documentary stamps, are due by 9:00 a.m. (24 hours) the following business day.
answers.quote: If you are the successful bidder, your bid amount, plus recording fees and documentary stamps, are due by 9:00 a.m. (24 hours) the following business day

answers.answer: The Clerk's FAQ does not list surviving liens: the bidder must research the property, and a lien or encumbrance found is a question for legal counsel before bidding.
answers.quote: What liens or encumbrances survive against a property after it is sold at a Tax Deed Sale? The bidder must do their own research on the property. If a lien/encumbrance is found then please seek legal counsel as to the validity of the lien/encumbrance prior to bidding.

answers.source_title: Clerk of Court - Tax Deed Services (Frequently Asked Questions)
answers.office: Charlotte County Clerk of the Circuit Court & County Comptroller
answers.answer: The Clerk's FAQ states that a tax deed sale purchase does not warrant or guarantee clear and marketable title; property is sold Buyer Beware and could be subject to liens and encumbrances.
answers.quote: Do I get a clear title with a Tax Deed? The purchase of a Tax Deed Sale does not warrant or guarantee clear and marketable title. Property is sold as "Buyer Beware" and could be subject to liens and encumbrances.

answers.source_title: Clerk of Court - Tax Deed Services (Frequently Asked Questions)

answers.quote: In order to purchase any of these parcels you must pay the original bid, any additional years taxes, and the Clerk of Court fees. For tax information, please contact our office at (941)743-1350. For Clerk of the Courts fees and information please call (941)637-2130.

answers.source_title: Charlotte County Tax Collector - Delinquent Taxes
answers.answer: Beginning on or before June 1st the Tax Collector holds a certificate sale over the Internet; each parcel is auctioned in the advertised order starting at 18% and bid down, and any item not bid on is struck to the County. A registration form must be completed online for each bidder.
answers.quote: Beginning on or before June 1st, the Tax Collector is required by law to hold a Tax Certificate Sale. ... Each parcel is auctioned in the order listed in the advertisement. The bidder begins at 18% (the maximum rate) and is bid down. The winning bidder's number and rate of interest bid are recorded. Any item not bid on is struck to the County. ... A registration form must be completed online for each bidder, with name, address, phone number, and tax-payer identification or social security number.

answers.source_title: Charlotte County Tax Collector - Delinquent Taxes
answers.answer: A county certificate costs the original certificate amount plus interest to the date of purchase, plus a $6.25 administrative fee, and a transfer costs $2.25 per certificate.
answers.quote: The purchase price is the amount of the original certificate plus interest due to the date of purchase, plus $6.25 administrative fee. ... There is a $2.25 transfer fee per certificate.

answers.source_title: Charlotte County Tax Collector - Delinquent Taxes
answers.answer: The Tax Collector names three risks: a correction that lowers or cancels the certificate (refunded at 8% or the bid rate, whichever is less), a property value drop that makes a sale cost more than the land is worth, and a landowner bankruptcy that stops enforcement of the lien.
answers.quote: There are three possible risks to consider: ... If there is a correction to the original taxes levied which would decrease the certificate value or cancel the certificate ... with 8% interest or rate of interest bid, whichever is less ... If the property value drops significantly in subsequent tax years, it may cost more to bring the property to sale than the value gained by owning the property. If the landowner enters into bankruptcy, the certificate holder is prevented from enforcing the lien

answers.source_title: Charlotte County Tax Collector - Delinquent Taxes
answers.answer: County held certificates are available for purchase on Lien Hub, and the lien is transferred to the buyer at 18%. Certificates may also be transferred for a $2.25 fee per certificate with a notarized transfer form and a valid bidder number.
answers.quote: Yes, County held certificates are available for purchase on Lien Hub . When someone buys a county certificate, the lien is transferred to the buyer. ... The interest rate of the purchased certificate is 18%. ... Certificates may be transferred. There is a $2.25 transfer fee per certificate. The certificate transfer form must be filled out properly and notarized. You must have a valid bidder number.

answers.source_title: Charlotte County Tax Collector - Delinquent Taxes
answers.answer: The Tax Collector says this is not a risk free investment and to check out the property before investing.
answers.quote: This is NOT a risk free investment. Be careful and check out the property before you invest any money.

answers.source_title: Welcome to Clay County Tax Collector (Tax Certificates page)
answers.office: Clay County Tax Collector - tax department
answers.answer: The Clay County Tax Collector's tax department answers questions about certificates at (904) 284-6329.
answers.quote: For information, contact the tax department at (904) 284-6329.

answers.source_title: Welcome to Clay County Tax Collector (Tax Certificates page)
answers.office: Clay County Tax Collector - tax department
answers.answer: Certificate bidding begins at an 18% interest rate and is bid down until the certificate is sold to the lowest bidder, and interest is paid at the winning bid rate.
answers.quote: Certificate bidding begins at an 18% interest rate and is bid down until the certificate is sold to the lowest bidder. Interest is paid at the rate of the winning bid.

answers.source_title: Welcome to Clay County Tax Collector (Tax Certificates page)
answers.office: Clay County Tax Collector - tax department
answers.answer: The certificate amount is the unpaid real estate taxes and non ad valorem assessments, including a 3% penalty, a 5% Tax Collector's commission, and additional fees.
answers.quote: The amount of the certificate is the sum of the unpaid real estate taxes and the non ad valorem assessments, including 3% penalty, 5% Tax Collector's commission, and additional fees.

answers.source_title: Welcome to Clay County Tax Collector (Tax Certificates page)
answers.office: Clay County Tax Collector - tax department
answers.answer: Any tax certificate can be cancelled or reduced if errors, omissions, or double assessments are made, and certificates expire seven years from the first day of the sale.
answers.quote: Tax Certificates are dated as of the first day of the tax certificate sale and expire seven (7) years from that date. Any tax certificate can be cancelled or reduced if errors, omissions, or double assessments are made.

answers.source_title: Welcome to Clay County Tax Collector (Tax Certificates page)
answers.office: Clay County Tax Collector - tax department

answers.quote: Tax Certificates not sold at the on-line auction may be purchased through ... For information, contact the tax department at (904) 284-6329.

answers.source_title: Tax Deeds (DeSoto County Clerk of Court)
answers.office: DeSoto County Clerk of Court - Tax Deed Department
answers.answer: The Tax Deed Department of the DeSoto County Clerk of Court answers questions about list purchases at (863) 993-4876.
answers.quote: To Purchase Property from the List of Lands Available, contact the DeSoto County Clerk of Court, Tax Deed Department at (863) 993-4876

answers.source_title: Tax Deeds (DeSoto County Clerk of Court)
answers.office: DeSoto County Clerk of Court - Tax Deed Department
answers.answer: A buyer contacts the Tax Deed Department to ask the current cost. 90 days after the date of sale any individual, county, or other unit of government may purchase from the list.
answers.quote: To Purchase Property from the List of Lands Available, contact the DeSoto County Clerk of Court, Tax Deed Department at (863) 993-4876 to ask about the current cost of purchasing the property. ... 90 days after the date of sale, any individual, county, or other units of government may purchase property from the List of Lands Available.

answers.source_title: Tax Deeds (DeSoto County Clerk of Court)
answers.office: DeSoto County Clerk of Court - Tax Deed Department
answers.answer: The total cost includes the opening bid at the time of the auction, past due taxes, the costs to bring the property to sale, one-half of the assessed value if homestead exempt, all taxes since the auction, accrued interest, and the costs to issue and record the Tax Deed including documentary stamps.
answers.quote: The total cost will include: Opening bid at the time of the auction Past due taxes Plus the costs required to bring the property to sale One-half of the assessed value, pursuant to F.S. 197.502(6)(c), if homestead exempt All taxes incurred since the auction Accrued interest Costs to issue and record the Tax Deed, including documentary stamps.

answers.source_title: Tax Deeds (DeSoto County Clerk of Court)
answers.office: DeSoto County Clerk of Court - Tax Deed Department
answers.answer: On top of the opening bid, the total includes all taxes incurred since the auction, accrued interest, and the costs to issue and record the Tax Deed, including documentary stamps.
answers.quote: All taxes incurred since the auction Accrued interest Costs to issue and record the Tax Deed, including documentary stamps.

answers.source_title: Tax Deeds (DeSoto County Clerk of Court)
answers.office: DeSoto County Clerk of Court - Tax Deed Department
answers.answer: The purchase of a tax deed does not warrant or guarantee a clear and marketable title, and neither the Clerk nor the Tax Collector warrants or guarantees one.
answers.quote: The purchase of a tax deed does not warrant or guarantee a clear and marketable title. Neither the Clerk of Circuit Court nor the Tax Collector warrants or guarantees a clear and marketable title.

answers.source_title: Lands Available for Taxes | Dixie County Clerk of Court
answers.office: Dixie County Clerk of Court & Comptroller
answers.answer: The Dixie County Clerk of Court & Comptroller's mailing address is P.O. Box 1206, Cross City, Florida 32628, and its phone number is (352) 498-1200.
answers.quote: Mailing Address: P.O. Box 1206 Cross City, Florida 32628 Phone Number: (352) 498-1200

answers.source_title: Lands Available for Taxes | Dixie County Clerk of Court
answers.office: Dixie County Clerk of Court & Comptroller
answers.answer: List properties must be bought from the Clerk of Court in person, first-come, first-served; they are not sold online. The purchaser provides the information for the new deed.
answers.quote: You are required to purchase these properties from the Clerk of Court in person. It is on a first-come, first-served basis. We do not sell these properties online. ... The purchaser will provide information for the new deed.

answers.source_title: Lands Available for Taxes | Dixie County Clerk of Court
answers.office: Dixie County Clerk of Court & Comptroller
answers.answer: The Total Purchase Price posted is good for the month indicated. The purchaser also pays 1/2 of the Homestead Assessed Value to the Clerk of Court at purchase, if applicable.
answers.quote: The Total Purchase Price posted is good for the month indicated and is payable in full, to the Clerk of Court with a Certified/Cashier’s Check, at the time of purchase. ... The Purchaser is responsible for paying 1/2 of the Homestead Assessed Value of the property. This is payable in full to the Clerk of Court at the time of purchase (if applicable).

answers.source_title: Lands Available for Taxes | Dixie County Clerk of Court
answers.office: Dixie County Clerk of Court & Comptroller
answers.answer: Recording Fees, Document Prep Fees, and DOC Stamps are not included in the posted price and are paid at purchase. The purchaser is also responsible for Current Taxes, which may not be included and are payable directly to the Tax Collector.
answers.quote: There are Recording Fees, Document Prep Fees, and DOC Stamps that must be paid in full to the Clerk of the Court with a Certified/Cashier’s Check at the time of purchase. These fees are not included in the total purchase price posted. ... The Purchaser is responsible for paying the Current Taxes. These may not be included in the total purchase price posted and are payable directly to the Tax Collector.

answers.source_title: Lands Available for Taxes | Dixie County Clerk of Court
answers.office: Dixie County Clerk of Court & Comptroller
answers.answer: Payment in full is made to the Clerk of Court with a Certified/Cashier's Check at the time of purchase; electronic payments and wire transfers are not accepted. The tax deed is then recorded and mailed with the receipt.
answers.quote: The purchaser will make payment in full to the Clerk of Court with a Certified/Cashier’s Check at the time of purchase. The purchase is receipted, and the tax deed is typed and recorded. ... We do not accept electronic payments and/or wire transfers for purchases from the List of Lands Available for Taxes.

answers.source_title: Lands Available for Taxes | Dixie County Clerk of Court
answers.office: Dixie County Clerk of Court & Comptroller
answers.answer: The clerk's page says it is always in the buyer's best interest to do due diligence on the process and on the listed properties before purchase. A property redeemed before sale is removed from the list and stays with the owner of record.
answers.quote: It is always in your best interest to do your due diligence regarding this process and on the properties listed for sale before purchase. If a property has been redeemed, before sale from the LOLA, the property will be removed from the List of Lands, and the current owner of record retains ownership of said property.

answers.source_title: Duvalclerk.gov - Tax Deed Files / Tax Deeds
answers.office: Duval County Clerk of the Circuit and County Courts - Tax Deeds Department
answers.answer: The Clerk's Tax Deeds Department is in Room 1054 of the Duval County Courthouse; Lands Available statement requests go to ask.taxdeeds@duvalclerk.com.
answers.quote: these forms of payment must be delivered to the Clerk’s Office in Room 1054 of the Duval County Courthouse. ... email the completed form to ask.taxdeeds@duvalclerk.com

answers.source_title: Duvalclerk.gov - Tax Deed Files / Tax Deeds
answers.answer: The Clerk posts the sale date and property list 30 days before the auction under "auction calendar" on the auction website, and advertises each sale once a week for four consecutive weeks.
answers.quote: Our office posts the sale date and a list of properties 30 days before the auction. You can find this list on the Tax Deed auction website under “auction calendar.” ... The Clerk's Office is required by Florida law to advertise each sale once a week for four consecutive weeks prior to the public auction.

answers.source_title: Duvalclerk.gov - Tax Deed Files / Tax Deeds
answers.answer: Sales are held online on the Clerk's auction website, duval.realtaxdeed.com.
answers.quote: Sales are held on our auction website, duval.realtaxdeed.com in accordance with Section 197.542(4)(a), Florida Statutes.

answers.source_title: Duvalclerk.gov - Tax Deed Files / Tax Deeds
answers.answer: Bidders register with the auction website, duval.realtaxdeed.com, and place the required deposit in order to bid.
answers.quote: You can register with the auction website, duval.realtaxdeed.com and place the required deposit in order to bid.

answers.source_title: Duvalclerk.gov - Tax Deed Files / Tax Deeds
answers.answer: The high bidder posts a non-refundable deposit of five percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, no later than 4:00 p.m. the day before the sale.
answers.quote: the high bidder will be asked to post with the clerk a non-refundable deposit of five percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater. The deposit will be applied to the sale price at the time of full payment. This deposit must be placed no later than 4:00 p.m. the day BEFORE the sale.

answers.source_title: Duvalclerk.gov - Tax Deed Files / Tax Deeds
answers.answer: Winning bidders pay their bid amounts and deed filing fees by 4:00 p.m. the next business day, by cashier's check, certified check, bank wire or money order; failure means a ban from future auctions and forfeiture of the deposit.
answers.quote: Winning bidders must pay their bid amounts and all fees for filing their deeds by 4:00 p.m. the next business day after the sale. Payments may be made by cashier’s check, certified check, bank wire, or money order in the Tax Deeds Department located in the Duval County Courthouse. Failure to do so will result in being banned from future Tax Deed auctions and a forfeiture of your deposit.

answers.source_title: Duvalclerk.gov - Tax Deed Files / Tax Deeds
answers.answer: The successful bidder also pays a Recording fee of $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each additional page, a Proof of Publication fee of $18.50, and Documentary Stamps based on the high bid.
answers.quote: you will also be required to pay Recording, Proof of Publication and Documentary Stamp fees. The Recording fee is $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each additional page. Proof of Publication fee is $18.50. Documentary Stamps are based on the high bid.

answers.source_title: Duvalclerk.gov - Tax Deed Files / Tax Deeds
answers.answer: The Clerk's Office cannot guarantee clear title. To obtain clear title the buyer will have to file a "Quiet-Title" suit in the Civil Court system, at fees above the purchase price.
answers.quote: The Clerk's Office cannot guarantee clear title to these properties. ... To obtain clear title, you will have to file a “Quiet-Title” suit in the Civil Court system. The fees required to file this suit are above and beyond the bidder’s purchase price.

answers.source_title: Duvalclerk.gov - Tax Deed Files / Tax Deeds
answers.answer: The Clerk calls the sale a "buyer-beware" situation and says it is the bidder's responsibility to search the title for any liens recorded against the property; parcels are sold "as-is".
answers.quote: All parcels are sold in "as-is" condition. It is the bidder's responsibility to search the title for any liens that may be recorded against the property. ... This is a “buyer-beware” situation.

answers.source_title: LANDS AVAILABLE FOR TAXES - Frequently Asked Questions (Duval County Clerk)
answers.answer: The Duval County Clerk's Tax Deeds Department handles the list: e-mail Ask.TaxDeeds@DuvalClerk.com or call (904) 255-1916, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Monday - Friday.
answers.quote: Completed forms may be submitted by email to Ask.TaxDeeds@DuvalClerk.com. ... please contact us between 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Monday - Friday at (904) 255-1916.

answers.source_title: LANDS AVAILABLE FOR TAXES - Frequently Asked Questions (Duval County Clerk)
answers.answer: Complete the Statement Request for Lands Available form and submit it by e-mail or in person; the Clerk calculates the purchase cost. Properties are not held for anyone and sell first come, first served.
answers.quote: please complete the Statement Request for Lands Available form. ... Completed forms may be submitted by email to Ask.TaxDeeds@DuvalClerk.com. Forms may also be submitted in person in Room 1054 of the Duval County Courthouse. After the Clerk receives your Statement Request, we will calculate the amount it will cost to purchase the requested property.

answers.source_title: LANDS AVAILABLE FOR TAXES - Frequently Asked Questions (Duval County Clerk)
answers.answer: After the County's first 90 days, anyone may buy for the opening bid, subsequent omitted taxes and any accrued interest. The statement amount must be paid within the month it is requested, because the figures are based on monthly interest.
answers.quote: After that initial 90 period has elapsed, anyone may purchase the land for the opening bid, subsequent omitted taxes, and any accrued interest. ... This amount must be paid within the month that statement is requested, as these figures are calculated based on monthly interest accrued.

answers.source_title: LANDS AVAILABLE FOR TAXES - Frequently Asked Questions (Duval County Clerk)
answers.answer: Documentary stamps and recording fees are also assessed and appear on the purchase statement.
answers.quote: Documentary stamps and recording fees are also assessed and will be reflected on the purchase statement.

answers.source_title: LANDS AVAILABLE FOR TAXES - Frequently Asked Questions (Duval County Clerk)
answers.answer: The Statement Request for Lands Available form; at a minimum it should include your name, phone number, the Tax Deed number and the real estate number.
answers.quote: please complete the Statement Request for Lands Available form. When completing the form, at a minimum please include your name, phone Number, the Tax Deed number, and real estate number

answers.source_title: LANDS AVAILABLE FOR TAXES - Frequently Asked Questions (Duval County Clerk)
answers.answer: Pay the total on the statement before its deadline (the last business day of that month) at the Tax Deeds Department with cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order payable to the Clerk of the Circuit Court, or by mail with a copy of the statement.
answers.quote: The deadline is the last business day of the month the request is processed. ... with cash, a cashier's check, a certified check, or money order made payable to the Clerk of the Circuit Court for the total amount of the statement, prior to the deadline. Payment may also be submitted by mail, along with a copy of your statement

answers.office: Duval County Tax Collector - Tax Department
answers.answer: The 2026 Duval Tax Certificate Sale was set for May 27th, 2026, with registration opening May 8th, 2026. A deposit of $100 or 10% of the total amount to be bid, whichever is greater, is required, and full payment minus the deposit is due within 48 hours after the sale ends.
answers.quote: The 2026 Duval Tax Certificate Sale will be May 27th, 2026. Registration opens May 8th, 2026 at ... A deposit of $100 or 10% of the total amount you want to bid, whichever is greater, is required. ... Full payment (minus your deposit) is due within 48 hours after the sale ends.

answers.source_title: Tax Collector - Tax Sale, Certificates, and Tax Deeds – A Guide for Investors (City of Jacksonville / Duval County)
answers.office: Duval County Tax Collector - Tax Department
answers.answer: Bidders post a deposit of $100 or 10% of the total amount they want to bid, whichever is greater, received 5 business days before the sale; they can win certificates up to 10 times the deposit. Refunds for unused deposits are issued within 14 business days.
answers.quote: A deposit of $100 or 10% of the total amount you want to bid, whichever is greater, is required. ... Deposits must be received 5 business days before the sale ... You can only win certificates up to your deposit limit x10 ... Refunds for unused deposits will be issued within 14 business days

answers.source_title: Tax Collector - Tax Sale, Certificates, and Tax Deeds – A Guide for Investors (City of Jacksonville / Duval County)
answers.office: Duval County Tax Collector - Tax Department
answers.answer: The Tax Collector warns of potential risks in certificate purchases and says all purchases are final. A certificate not used for a tax deed application within 7 years of issuance expires and becomes worthless, and a Tax Deed is not a Warranty Deed.
answers.quote: There are potential risks associated with tax certificate purchases. Research tax certificates before purchasing. All purchases of county held tax certificates are final. ... If you do not apply for a tax deed within 7 years of issuance , the certificate expires and becomes worthless ... A Tax Deed is not a Warranty Deed .

answers.source_title: Tax Collector - Tax Sale, Certificates, and Tax Deeds – A Guide for Investors (City of Jacksonville / Duval County)
answers.office: Duval County Tax Collector - Tax Department
answers.answer: Unsold certificates from previous years can be bought directly at lienhub.com/county/duval, and all purchases of county held tax certificates are final.
answers.quote: Unsold certificates from previous years can be purchased directly at: ... lienhub.com/county/duval ... All purchases of county held tax certificates are final.

answers.source_title: Tax Collector - Tax Sale, Certificates, and Tax Deeds – A Guide for Investors (City of Jacksonville / Duval County)
answers.office: Duval County Tax Collector - Tax Department
answers.answer: The Tax Collector says it is the buyer's sole responsibility to research any certificates, that property and tax information is available by clicking the Account or Parcel Number on the auction site, and to research advertised items carefully before bidding.
answers.quote: It is your sole responsibility to research any tax lien certificates you intend to buy. You can see additional property and tax information for any item by clicking on the Account or Parcel Number on the auction web site. Research any advertised items carefully before submitting bids.

answers.answer: The Lee County Tax Collector's phone number is (239) 533.6000.

answers.source_title: Tax Certificate Sale - Fort Myers, FL - Tax Collectors Office (Lee County Tax Collector)
answers.answer: The sale is competitive, with interest bids starting at 18% and going down in 0.25% steps; the certificate goes to the bidder accepting the lowest rate.
answers.quote: The sale is operated on a competitive bid basis with interest bids beginning at 18% and progressing downward in 0.25% increments. The tax certificate is issued to the bidder that will accept the lowest rate of interest.

answers.source_title: Tax Certificate Sale - Fort Myers, FL - Tax Collectors Office (Lee County Tax Collector)
answers.answer: A county held certificate costs its face value, accrued interest, and a $6.25 processing fee. Transferring a certificate costs $2.25 per certificate with an Endorsement form.
answers.quote: The cost to purchase a county held certificate is the face value of the certificate, accrued interest, and a $6.25 processing fee. ... Those seeking to transfer the tax certificates they hold, are required to complete and submit an Endorsement form to the Tax Collector’s Office and include a check, cashiers’ check, or money order in the amount of $2.25 per certificate to be transferred.

answers.source_title: Tax Certificate Sale - Fort Myers, FL - Tax Collectors Office (Lee County Tax Collector)
answers.answer: The Tax Collector says there are risks in buying certificates and does not guarantee the value or condition of the property; a certificate can be cancelled or reduced to correct errors, omissions, or double assessments, or by court order.
answers.quote: There are risks involved when purchasing tax certificates. The Tax Collector assumes no liability and does not guarantee the value, nor the condition of the property on which the certificate is issued. ... A certificate could be cancelled or reduced for various reasons such as to correct errors, omission, double assessments or when ordered by a court.

answers.source_title: Tax Certificate Sale - Fort Myers, FL - Tax Collectors Office (Lee County Tax Collector)
answers.answer: Unsold certificates are held by the county and may be bought after the sale before redemption or a tax deed. Holders transfer certificates by submitting an Endorsement form with $2.25 per certificate.
answers.quote: Certificates that are not sold at the tax certificate sale are held by the county. They may be purchased after the tax certificate sale prior to redemption or execution of a tax deed. ... Those seeking to transfer the tax certificates they hold, are required to complete and submit an Endorsement form to the Tax Collector’s Office and include a check, cashiers’ check, or money order in the amount of $2.25 per certificate to be transferred.

answers.source_title: Tax Deeds | Marion County Clerk of Court and Comptroller
answers.answer: A non-refundable deposit must be in the bidder's account by the Monday before the auction: $200 per parcel when the winning bid is $4000.00 or less, otherwise 5% of the winning bid.

answers.source_title: Tax Deeds | Marion County Clerk of Court and Comptroller

answers.answer: The Okaloosa County Tax Collector's service line is (850) 651-7300.

answers.source_title: Tax Certificate Sale - Okaloosa County Tax Collector
answers.answer: Certificates are sold in the advertised order, with bidding starting at 18 percent and going down in quarter-percent steps; each goes to the lowest rate, ties are settled by random number, and unbid items are struck to the county. Registration, bidding and awards all take place on the auction web site.
answers.quote: Certificates are sold in the order advertised. Bidding begins at 18 percent (the maximum rate) and bids down in increments of one-quarter of one percent. Each certificate is sold individually to the bidder offering the lowest interest rate. In the case of a tie at the lowest rate, the winner will be selected using a random number generator in the auction software. Items that receive no bids are "struck" to the county and become county-held certificates. ... All activity related to registration, bidding, and certificate awards takes place on the auction web site.

answers.source_title: Tax Certificate Sale - Okaloosa County Tax Collector
