answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2153
answers.note: Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).
answers.answer: The tax collector advertises the tax lien for sale by public auction and issues a tax lien certificate in favor of the winning bidder, recorded in the mortgage records.
answers.quote: the tax collector will advertise for sale by public auction the tax lien and that the tax collector will issue in favor of the winning bidder and record in the mortgage records a tax lien certificate.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154
answers.answer: The tax collector advertises the tax lien auction on or before May first of the year after the taxes were assessed, or as soon as possible after that. Bidding is held on weekdays, opening no earlier than 8:00 a.m. and closing no later than 8:00 p.m.
answers.quote: The tax collector shall advertise for sale by public auction the tax lien on or before May first of the year following the year in which the taxes were assessed, or as soon thereafter as possible. ... The tax lien auction shall be conducted on any weekday, with bidding opening not earlier than 8:00 a.m. and closing no later than 8:00 p.m.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154
answers.answer: The law allows a tax lien auction to be held online or electronically over several days; bids placed before the auction opens are void.
answers.quote: If a tax lien auction is conducted by using an online or electronic bidding process that is conducted over the course of multiple days, bids may be placed on any day at any time on any tax lien upon which bidding has not closed, provided that all bidding closes on a weekday within the hours prescribed in this Subsection. Any bid received prior to the opening of the auction shall be null and void.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2153
answers.note: State law refers to registered tax lien auction participants but does not set a registration procedure; check the parish tax collector.
answers.where_to_look: See Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2153.

links.title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2153

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2153
answers.answer: The tax collector may require registered participants to pay a deposit, not to exceed one thousand dollars, before the auction. The winner's deposit is applied to the sale price; other bidders' deposits are returned no later than fourteen days after the auction closes.
answers.quote: The tax collector may require all registered tax lien auction participants to provide a deposit, not to exceed one thousand dollars, prior to the commencement of the tax lien auction. If a deposit is required, the deposit of the winning bidder shall be applied toward the sale price at the time of purchase. A deposit from a nonwinning bidder shall be returned or refunded to the depositor no later than fourteen days after the close of the auction.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154
answers.answer: The auction price is the face value of the tax lien certificate. Bidders compete on the monthly interest rate: the maximum is one percent per month, bids go down in steps of one-tenth of one percent, and no bid below seven-tenths of one percent per month is accepted.
answers.quote: The auction price shall be the face value of the tax lien certificate. ... Subject to a maximum bid of one percent per month, bidders may submit bids reducing the monthly interest rate in increments of one-tenth of one percent or an integral multiple thereof. ... no bid shall be accepted that purports to reduce the rate of monthly interest below seven-tenths of one percent.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2153
answers.answer: The statutory advertisement says the sale is for cash or another payment method the tax collector accepts. The law quoted does not state a payment deadline.
answers.quote: At the auction, I will sell the tax lien to the winning bidder. The sale will be for cash or other payment method acceptable to the tax collector, in legal tender money of the United States.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154
answers.answer: The clerk of court's recording cost is included in the price paid at the auction and in the face value of the certificate.
answers.quote: The recording cost due to the clerk of court shall be included in the price paid at the tax lien auction and the face value of the tax lien certificate.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2266.1
answers.note: The winning bidder receives a tax lien certificate, not a deed (R.S. 47:2154(E)); property passes only through the judicial sale in R.S. 47:2267, executed by the sheriff. Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).
answers.answer: After the later of three years from recording the tax lien certificate or six months after the required post-auction notices, a certificate holder may sue to have the delinquent obligation and the lien recognized.
answers.quote: Upon the expiration of the later of three years from recordation of the tax lien certificate, or the tax sale certificate if R.S. 47:2201(B) is applicable, or six months after providing the notices required by R.S. 47:2156, a certificate holder may, by verified petition, institute in a court of competent jurisdiction

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2266.1
answers.answer: Anyone may extinguish the tax lien by paying the termination price to the tax collector until close of business on the thirtieth day after the last party is served in the certificate holder's enforcement suit.
answers.quote: Until close of business on the thirtieth day following the date on which the last party was served, or the next day that is not a legal holiday if the thirtieth day is a legal holiday, any person may cause the tax lien to be extinguished by delivering the termination price to the tax collector.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2268
answers.answer: A judicial sale to enforce the tax lien ends all interests in the property, except rights created by certain written instruments listed in the statute that were filed before the tax lien certificate was recorded.
answers.quote: a judicial sale pursuant to R.S. 47:2267 shall terminate all interests in the immovable property. B. The rights and obligations established or created by the following written instruments affecting immovable property shall not be terminated pursuant to this Chapter to the extent the interests remain effective against third persons and are filed with the appropriate recorder prior to the recordation of the tax lien certificate:

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154
answers.answer: If no one bids, the tax collector issues and records the tax lien certificate in favor of the political subdivision.
answers.quote: If there is no bidder, the tax collector shall issue and record the tax lien certificate in favor of the political subdivision.

answers.note: Sales authority: R.S. 47:2201(A)(1). Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).
answers.answer: Adjudicated property is property whose tax sale title a political subdivision acquired under R.S. 47:2196 before January 1, 2026.
answers.quote: "Adjudicated property" means property of which tax sale title is acquired by a political subdivision pursuant to R.S. 47:2196 prior to January 1, 2026.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2203
answers.answer: Any person may start the public sale of adjudicated property by making a written request to the political subdivision and depositing the amount it sets to cover the sale's expenses, including advertising and appraisals.
answers.quote: any person may initiate the public sale of adjudicated property or property subject to a tax lien certificate held by a political subdivision by making a written request to the political subdivision and depositing an amount determined by the political subdivision to be sufficient to cover the expenses of the sale, including advertising, appraisals, and other costs associated with the sale.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2202
answers.answer: The political subdivision may sell to the highest bidder without a minimum bid or appraisal. If it sets a dollar minimum bid, that minimum must be at least the statutory impositions, governmental liens and costs of sale.
answers.quote: The governing authority of each political subdivision may elect to sell adjudicated property at a public sale to the highest bidder without setting a minimum bid or requiring an appraisal. (2) If the governing authority elects to set a dollar amount as a minimum bid for the public sale of adjudicated property, the minimum bid shall be no less than the total amount of statutory impositions, governmental liens, and costs of sale.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2207
answers.answer: The buyer files the act of sale or donation and pays all filing fees.
answers.quote: A transferee of immovable property in accordance with this Subpart shall be responsible for filing the act of sale or donation and payment of all filing fees.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2203
answers.answer: Any person may start the public sale of adjudicated property by making a written request to the political subdivision and depositing an amount the political subdivision sets to cover the expenses of the sale. If the depositor is not the highest bidder, the deposit is returned.
answers.quote: Provided that all other requirements are satisfied, any person may initiate the public sale of adjudicated property or property subject to a tax lien certificate held by a political subdivision by making a written request to the political subdivision and depositing an amount determined by the political subdivision to be sufficient to cover the expenses of the sale, including advertising, appraisals, and other costs associated with the sale. ... Should the depositor at the sale fail to be the highest bidder, the money deposited shall be returned to him.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2207
answers.note: Replaces the 2026-10-29 NOT_VERIFIED row; the parish ordinance sets the actual payment terms (see the East Baton Rouge row).
answers.answer: The statutory act of sale is a non-warranty cash sale reciting that the purchaser has paid the price in cash to the political subdivision; the transferee files the act of sale for recordation and pays all filing fees. The statute sets no payment deadline.
answers.quote: NON-WARRANTY CASH SALE ... cash, which Purchaser has paid to Seller. ... The transferee shall file the act of sale or donation for recordation in the conveyance records of the parish in which the property is located and shall be responsible for the payment of all filing fees.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2207
answers.answer: The political subdivision's only warranty is against eviction resulting from its own prior sale; otherwise the sale is without any warranty, even as to return or reduction of the price.
answers.quote: The only warranty owed by the political subdivision shall be a warranty against eviction resulting from a prior alienation by the political subdivision. Otherwise, all sales and donations shall be without warranty, either expressed or implied, even as to return or reduction of the purchase price

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2208
answers.answer: For a sale of adjudicated property, filing the affidavit required by R.S. 47:2208(A) cancels the statutory impositions of all political subdivisions then due, all governmental liens, and the interests, liens, mortgages and other encumbrances recorded against the property and listed in the affidavit.
answers.quote: With respect to a sale of adjudicated property, the filing of the affidavit provided in Subsection A of this Section shall operate as a cancellation, termination, release, or erasure of record of all statutory impositions of all political subdivisions then due and owing, of all governmental liens, and of all interests, liens, mortgages, privileges, and other encumbrances recorded against the property sold and listed in the affidavit.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2207
answers.answer: The political subdivision owes only a warranty against eviction resulting from its own prior alienation; otherwise sales are without any warranty, express or implied.
answers.quote: The only warranty owed by the political subdivision shall be a warranty against eviction resulting from a prior alienation by the political subdivision. Otherwise, all sales and donations shall be without warranty, either expressed or implied, even as to return or reduction of the purchase price

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2207
answers.answer: Sales of adjudicated property are without warranty, even as to return or reduction of the purchase price.
answers.quote: Otherwise, all sales and donations shall be without warranty, either expressed or implied, even as to return or reduction of the purchase price

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2207
answers.answer: State law makes every sale of adjudicated property without warranty, even as to return or reduction of the price, including defects and fitness for any purpose; the waiver applies whether or not it appears in the act of sale or is brought to the buyer's attention.
answers.quote: Otherwise, all sales and donations shall be without warranty, either expressed or implied, even as to return or reduction of the purchase price, including without limitation the warranty against redhibitory defects or vices and the warranty that the thing sold is reasonably fit for its ordinary purpose or the transferee's intended or particular purpose. These waivers or exclusions of warranties shall be self-operative regardless of whether the waivers or exclusions are contained in the act of sale or donation ... and regardless of whether they are brought to the attention of the transferee.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154
answers.note: Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).
answers.answer: At the tax lien auction the winning bidder receives a tax lien certificate, recorded in the parish mortgage records, which is prima facie evidence of the lien and its assignment to the holder.
answers.quote: No later than thirty days after conclusion of the tax lien auction, the tax collector shall issue and file in the mortgage records of the parish in which the property is situated a tax lien certificate in favor of the winning bidder. ... The tax lien certificate shall be prima facie evidence of the validity of the tax lien and the assignment to the person named thereon.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154
answers.answer: Bidding is on the monthly interest rate that will accrue on the certificate's face value; the lowest rate wins, and a tie goes to the bidder who bid first.
answers.quote: The subject of the competitive bidding shall be the monthly rate at which interest will accrue on the face value of the tax lien certificate following its issuance. ... The bid that requires the assessment of interest at the lowest rate shall be declared the winner. If multiple bidders submit the same lowest bid, the winner shall be the first in time to submit the bid.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154
answers.answer: Interest accrues on the certificate's face value at the monthly rate set by the winning bid, or at one percent per month when the political subdivision holds the certificate, in both cases without compounding.
answers.quote: Upon the issuance of a tax lien certificate, interest shall accrue on the face value of the tax lien certificate at the monthly rate established by the winning bid at the tax lien auction. If the tax lien certificate is issued in favor of the political subdivision, interest shall accrue on the face value of the tax lien certificate at the rate of one percent per month. In both cases, interest shall be calculated on a noncompounding basis.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2155
answers.answer: The taxes, interest, penalties and costs may be paid at any time until thirty days after service of a petition to enforce the tax lien.
answers.quote: the statutory impositions, together with interest, penalties, and costs, may be paid at any time prior to the expiration of thirty days after service of a petition to enforce the tax lien.

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2267
answers.answer: A judgment for the certificate holder in an enforcement action under R.S. 47:2266.1 is executed by a writ of fieri facias under the Code of Civil Procedure (a judicial sale).
answers.quote: a judgment rendered in favor of the tax lien certificate holder in an action brought pursuant to R.S. 47:2266.1 shall be executed by a writ of fieri facias in accordance with the provisions of Title II of Book IV of the Code of Civil Procedure

answers.source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2155
answers.answer: An action to enforce the tax lien must be brought within seven years from recording the tax lien certificate in the parish mortgage records; after that the tax lien is extinguished.
answers.quote: An action to enforce the tax lien pursuant to R.S. 47:2266.1 shall be brought no later than seven years from the date that the tax lien certificate is recorded in the mortgage records of the parish in which the property is located. Upon the expiration of this time period, the tax lien shall be extinguished

answers.source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
answers.answer: Sales of adjudicated property are handled through the Office of the Parish Attorney, telephone (225) 389-3114.
answers.quote: Abandoned adjudicated property sales for the Parish are handled through the Office of the Parish Attorney. Questions concerning the sale process and procedures should be addressed to that office, telephone number (225) 389-3114

answers.source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
answers.note: The Parish Attorney's own page also links an open-data list and CivicSource; the memorandum states the City-Parish keeps no list.
answers.answer: First confirm that the property was adjudicated and is still adjudicated to the City-Parish (the City-Parish keeps no list of adjudicated properties), then call the Parish Attorney's Office to confirm it is still available.
answers.quote: you must first determine that the property in which you are interested has in fact been adjudicated, and is still adjudicated, to the City-Parish. The City-Parish does not maintain a roster/ list/ database of properties that are adjudicated. ... you must call the Parish Attorney's Office so that someone in our office can confirm that the property is still currently available

answers.source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
answers.answer: Offers need not equal the appraised value or the taxes and public liens; the Metropolitan Council considers those amounts when deciding whether to accept or reject the offer.
answers.quote: Offers do not have to equal or exceed either the appraised value or the amount of taxes and public liens. However, these amounts will be considered by the Metropolitan Council at a regularly scheduled meeting in which it will be determined whether to accept or reject your offer.

answers.source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
answers.answer: Advanced costs are at least $500 per property, and some properties have additional costs; this fee is not part of the sale price. The buyer also pays all fees and expenses to record the sale documents.
answers.quote: This amount will be a MINIMUM of $500. However, each individual property may have additional amounts due for costs. ... This fee is not part of the sales price that is ultimately paid to buy the property. ... You are responsible for all fees and expense to record these documents.

answers.source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
answers.answer: To open a file: a completed 'Request to Purchase Adjudicated Property' form, the two-page tax print and current tax bill from the Sheriff, and a certified check or money order for advanced costs for each property, among other items.
answers.quote: A completed "Request to Purchase Adjudicated Property" form . ... A copy of the two page tax print and the current tax bill for that particular property. You will obtain this from the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff. ... A certified check or money order for advanced costs for each piece of property you open a file on.

answers.source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
answers.answer: Advanced costs are paid by certified check or money order payable to the City of Baton Rouge (no personal checks or cash). The sale price is paid with certified funds at the closing.
answers.quote: NO PERSONAL CHECKS OR CASH can be accepted. Checks must be made payable to the "City of Baton Rouge." ... Please note that you will be required to pay the sales price with certified funds at the time of the sale.

answers.source_title: City of Baton Rouge / Parish of East Baton Rouge - Office of the Parish Attorney, Adjudicated Property memorandum
answers.office: Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division
answers.answer: The buyer pays the sales price with certified funds at the sale. The City-Parish reserves all mineral rights, with a waiver as to surface rights, and the sale is without any warranty, even as to return of the purchase price.
answers.quote: Please note that you will be required to pay the sales price with certified funds at the time of the sale. Please also note that the City-Parish shall reserve all mineral rights in and to the property conveyed, but with a waiver as to surface rights. The sale shall be without any warranty whatsoever, even as to the return of the purchase price.

answers.source_title: City of Baton Rouge / Parish of East Baton Rouge - Office of the Parish Attorney, Adjudicated Property memorandum
answers.office: Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division
answers.answer: The Parish Attorney will not open a file on property adjudicated for less than three years from recordation of the Act of Adjudication. The tax debtor or owner may redeem the property with the Sheriff at any time before the City-Parish sells it.
answers.quote: the tax debtor/owner of an adjudicated property has the right to redeem that property with the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff at any time prior to our sale of the property to you. ... We will not open a file for any property that has been adjudicated for less than three years from the date the Act of Adjudication was recorded.

answers.source_title: City of Baton Rouge / Parish of East Baton Rouge - Office of the Parish Attorney, Adjudicated Property memorandum
answers.office: Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division
answers.answer: The sale is without any warranty, even as to return of the purchase price. The Parish Attorney's Office gives the buyer a copy of La. R. S. 47:2208 on additional steps the buyer may elect to take regarding the title.
answers.quote: The sale shall be without any warranty whatsoever, even as to the return of the purchase price. ... The Parish Attorney's Office shall provide you a copy of La. R. S. 47:2208 concerning what additional steps you may elect to take regarding the title to the subject property.

answers.source_title: City of Baton Rouge / Parish of East Baton Rouge - Office of the Parish Attorney, Adjudicated Property memorandum
answers.office: Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division
answers.answer: The advanced costs are not applied to the purchase price and are not refunded if the Council rejects the offer or the buyer does not complete the sale. They are refunded only if the buyer is not the high bidder or the tax debtor redeems before the sale.
answers.quote: YOUR INITIAL PAYMENT OF COSTS SHALL NOT BE APPLIED TO THE PURCHASE PRICE. YOUR INITIAL CHECK FOR COSTS WILL NOT BE REFUNDED IF THE COUNCIL REJECTS YOUR OFFER, OR IF YOU ELECT NOT TO COMPLETE THE SALE FOR WHATEVER REASON. IT SHALL BE REFUNDED TO YOU ONLY IF: (a) YOU ARE NOT THE HIGH BIDDER, OR (b) IF THE TAX DEBTOR REDEEMS THE PROPERTY BEFORE THE SALE OF THE PROPERTY BY THE PARISH.

answers.source_title: City of Baton Rouge / Parish of East Baton Rouge - Office of the Parish Attorney, Adjudicated Property memorandum
answers.office: Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division
answers.answer: The memorandum calls the process complex and strongly advises consulting a private attorney, particularly one handling real estate. The City-Parish keeps no list of adjudicated property; buyers research the property with the Sheriff, the Clerk of Court and the Assessor.
answers.quote: The process of purchasing adjudicated property is complex. YOU ARE STRONGLY ADVISED TO CONSULT A PRIVATE ATTORNEY, PARTICULARLY ONE THAT HANDLES REAL ESTATE TRANSACTIONS. ... The City-Parish does not maintain a roster/ list/ database of properties that are adjudicated. You will need to research the property you are interested in with the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff

AUCTIONS.summary: A county treasurer's sale of tax-foreclosed parcels.

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
answers.answer: Property foreclosed for delinquent taxes is sold at auction by the foreclosing governmental unit (or its authorized agent) at one or more sales, which may include an online auction.
answers.quote: the foreclosing governmental unit, or its authorized agent, at the option of the foreclosing governmental unit, shall hold 1 or more property sales at 1 or more convenient locations at which property foreclosed by a judgment entered under section 78k will be sold by auction sale, which may include an auction sale conducted via an internet website.

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
answers.answer: Sales are held between the third Tuesday in July after the foreclosure judgment and the following first Tuesday in November.
answers.quote: beginning on the third Tuesday in July immediately succeeding the entry of the judgment under section 78k vesting absolute title to tax delinquent property in the foreclosing governmental unit and ending on the immediately succeeding first Tuesday in November, the foreclosing governmental unit, or its authorized agent, at the option of the foreclosing governmental unit, shall hold 1 or more property sales

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
answers.answer: Sales are held at one or more convenient locations and may include an auction conducted via an internet website.
answers.quote: shall hold 1 or more property sales at 1 or more convenient locations at which property foreclosed by a judgment entered under section 78k will be sold by auction sale, which may include an auction sale conducted via an internet website.

answers.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.note: Applies to auctions conducted through Tax-Sale.info, the platform many Michigan county treasurers use; the statute (MCL 211.78m) sets no registration or deposit rule, so counties that run their own sale set their own.
answers.answer: On Tax-Sale.info, bidders first create a free online user account; identity is verified during registration, so the information given must match a government issued ID.
answers.quote: How do I register for the auction? In order to participate in our online auctions, you must first create a free online user account. ... We will need to verify your identity during the registration process, so please use accurate information that matches your government issued ID.

answers.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.note: Applies to auctions conducted through Tax-Sale.info, the platform many Michigan county treasurers use; the statute (MCL 211.78m) sets no registration or deposit rule, so counties that run their own sale set their own.
answers.answer: On Tax-Sale.info, placing bids requires a $1000 pre-authorization on a major credit card, valid for 30-days; it is a hold rather than a charge, serves as a security deposit, and is collected against only if a winning bidder fails to pay.
answers.quote: To place bids, you must be logged into a valid active account and must provide a $1000 pre-authorization on a major credit card. Pre-authorization is valid for 30-days. This pre-authorization is not a charge, but rather a hold by your financial institution for up to 30 days, which allows you to bid and serves as a security deposit. This hold will only be collected against if you fail to pay for property that you win.

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
answers.note: At the final sale the minimum bid is not required; the county may set a reasonable opening bid to recover sale costs (MCL 211.78m(5)).
answers.answer: The minimum bid must include all delinquent taxes, interest, penalties and fees on the property, and may include the foreclosing governmental unit's additional expenses for forfeiture, foreclosure, maintenance, repair or remediation.
answers.quote: The minimum bid must include all of the delinquent taxes, interest, penalties, and fees due on the property, and may include any additional expenses incurred by the foreclosing governmental unit in connection with the forfeiture, foreclosure, maintenance, repair, or remediation of the property

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
answers.answer: The county must require full payment at the close of each day's bidding or by a date no more than 21 days after the sale.
answers.quote: The foreclosing governmental unit shall require full payment at the close of each day's bidding or by a date not more than 21 days after the sale.

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
answers.note: MCL 211.78m(10): 'The foreclosing governmental unit may charge a fee in excess of the minimum bid and any sale proceeds for the cost of recording a deed under this subsection.'
answers.answer: Before the property is conveyed, the buyer must give the county proof of paying the local tax collecting unit any property taxes owed on the property at the time of the sale.
answers.quote: Before the foreclosing governmental unit conveys a property sold at a sale, the purchaser shall provide the foreclosing governmental unit with proof of payment to the local tax collecting unit in which the property is located of any property taxes owed on the property at the time of the sale.

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
answers.note: Tax-Sale.info's FAQ says buyers at its Michigan auctions receive a quitclaim deed.
answers.answer: The deed must vest fee simple title in the highest bidder, unless the county finds a defect in the foreclosure or the sale is canceled.
answers.quote: The deed must vest fee simple title to the property in the person bidding the highest amount above the minimum bid, unless the foreclosing governmental unit discovers a defect in the foreclosure of the property under sections 78 to 78l or the sale is canceled under this subsection or subsection (5).

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78k - Michigan Legislature
answers.note: Former owners may instead claim remaining sale proceeds by filing a notice with the foreclosing governmental unit by the July 1 after foreclosure (MCL 211.78t(2)).
answers.answer: All redemption rights expire on the March 31 after the foreclosure judgment is entered, or 21 days after the judgment in a contested case.
answers.quote: All redemption rights to the property expire on the March 31 immediately succeeding the entry of a judgment foreclosing the property under this section, or in a contested case 21 days after the entry of a judgment foreclosing the property under this section.

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78k - Michigan Legislature
answers.note: 78k(5)(c) also keeps future installments of special assessments and environmental liens; 78m(12) cancels liens for demolition, safety repairs, debris removal and sewer or water charges as of the December 31 after the sale.
answers.answer: The foreclosure judgment extinguishes all existing recorded and unrecorded interests except, among others listed in the statute, a visible or recorded easement or right-of-way, private deed restrictions, and the interest of a lessee under a recorded oil or gas lease.
answers.quote: That all existing recorded and unrecorded interests in that property are extinguished, except a visible or recorded easement or right-of-way, private deed restrictions, interests of a lessee or an assignee of an interest of a lessee under a recorded oil or gas lease

answers.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.note: Applies to auctions conducted through Tax-Sale.info; the Michigan Department of Treasury notes many county treasurers hired Tax-Sale.info to conduct their auctions.
answers.answer: Tax-Sale.info says insuring tax reverted land is often more complicated than other purchases and some insurers are more willing than others to write a policy on it.
answers.quote: Insuring tax reverted lands will often be more complicated than with property purchased in other types of sale. Some insurers are more willing to write a policy on tax reverted property than others.

answers.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.note: Applies to auctions conducted through Tax-Sale.info; the Michigan Department of Treasury notes many county treasurers hired Tax-Sale.info to conduct their auctions.
answers.answer: Tax-Sale.info says occupants at the time of sale must be treated as tenants-holding-over and removed through formal eviction proceedings in District Court, not by force, threat or coercion.
answers.quote: Any occupants of the property at the time of sale must be treated as "tenants-holding-over" (like a tenant whose lease has expired). You must pursue formal eviction proceeds in the District Court. Removing occupants by force, threat, or coercion (shutting off the utilities or changing locks) can create major legal issues.

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
answers.answer: By the December 1 after the judgment, a list of all unsold property goes to the clerk of the city, village or township where it lies, which may object in writing to the transfer of any of it.
answers.quote: On or before December 1 immediately succeeding the entry of judgment under section 78k, a list of all property not previously sold by the foreclosing governmental unit under this section must be transferred to the clerk of the city, village, or township in which the property is located. The city, village, or township may object in writing to the transfer of 1 or more properties.

answers.note: Applies to property on which the authority obtained the expedited quiet title judgment. Property that reached the land bank through a tax foreclosure judgment carries the near-identical exceptions of MCL 211.78k(5) (see the Auctions ledger). MCL 124.756(5): a deed in lieu of foreclosure accepted by an authority does not impair other liens or interests unless the taxing jurisdictions approve.
answers.answer: After a land bank authority's expedited quiet title judgment, all liens against the property are extinguished except future installments of special assessments and liens recorded by the state or the authority under the natural resources and environmental protection act, and all other recorded and unrecorded interests are extinguished except a visible or recorded easement or right-of-way, private deed restrictions, plat restrictions, and governmental interests under that act.

answers.source_title: MCL - Section 124.759 - Michigan Legislature
answers.note: Whether a given parcel went through the expedited action is for the authority to state; MCL 124.757(2) requires an authority to inventory and classify its property according to title status and suitability for use. The statute does not say whether a buyer's title is insurable.
answers.answer: A land bank authority may bring an expedited quiet title and foreclosure action on property it holds; the circuit court's judgment specifies that fee simple title is vested absolutely in the authority without further rights of redemption and that the authority has good and marketable fee simple title, with the exceptions the statute lists.
answers.quote: An authority may initiate an expedited quiet title and foreclosure action under this section to quiet title to real property held by the authority or interests in tax reverted property held by the authority ... That fee simple title to property foreclosed by the judgment is vested absolutely in the authority, except as otherwise provided in subdivisions (c) and (e), without any further rights of redemption. ... That, except as otherwise provided in subdivisions (c) and (e), the authority has good and marketable fee simple title to the property.

answers.answer: Submit an offer online using Tax-Sale.info's form; once it is received and you are deemed eligible to buy, you are contacted to gather deed and payment information.
answers.quote: In order to purchase a property, a purchaser must submit an offer online by using this form . Once this form is received and a purchaser is deemed eligible to buy, they will be contacted to gather deed and payment information.

answers.source_title: Surplus Properties - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.answer: A $30 deed recording fee and a $20 processing fee are charged for each purchase; card payments carry a 2.75% fee.
answers.quote: There will be a $30 deed recording fee and a $20 processing fee for each purchase. Credit Card (with 2.75% Credit Card Fees applied), Cashiers Check and Wire Transfers are the only acceptable payments.

answers.source_title: Surplus Properties - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.answer: The buyer must not directly or indirectly hold more than a de minimis legal interest in any property with delinquent property taxes in the same county.
answers.quote: The person does not directly or indirectly hold more than a de minimis legal interest in any property with delinquent property taxes located in the same county as the property.

answers.source_title: Surplus Properties - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.note: Same page: 'Credit Card (with 2.75% Credit Card Fees applied), Cashiers Check and Wire Transfers are the only acceptable payments.'
answers.answer: Pay the full amount plus fees within 5 days of being deemed an eligible buyer.
answers.quote: Purchaser must pay full amount plus fees within 5 days of being deemed an eligible buyer.

answers.source_title: Surplus Properties - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.note: Tax-Sale.info lists 'Arenac Surplus 2026' among its surplus property sales.
answers.answer: There are no refunds on surplus properties.
answers.quote: Please perform your due diligence carefully, and be sure you fully understand what you are purchasing. There are no refunds.

answers.source_title: Surplus Properties - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.note: Tax-Sale.info lists 'Arenac Surplus 2026' among its surplus property sales.
answers.answer: Most surplus properties did not sell for a reason, which can include wetlands, lack of legal access, parcels too small or narrow to build on, terrain, or taxes and association fees exceeding the land's value; buyers are told to perform their due diligence carefully.
answers.quote: Be aware that most have reasons they did not sell, which can include wetlands, lack of legal access, parcels that are too small or narrow to build on, terrain challenges, or the annual taxes, property owners association (POA) fees or other costs may exceed the value of the land itself. ... Please perform your due diligence carefully, and be sure you fully understand what you are purchasing.

answers.quote: REGISTRATION Pre-registration is available at www.BippusUSA.com. Bidders are strongly encouraged to pre-register. The sale will not be delayed to accommodate on-site registrants. On-site registration will begin at 5:00 p.m. and the sale will begin promptly at 6:00 p.m. No bids will be accepted unless the bidder has registered and received a pre-numbered bid card. A valid driver’s license or state I.D. and social security number will be required to register. ... No individual or entity currently owing delinquent real property taxes to the Treasurer will be allowed to register.

answers.answer: Submit an offer online using Tax-Sale.info's form; once it is received and you are deemed eligible to buy, you are contacted to gather deed and payment information.

answers.source_title: Surplus Properties - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.answer: A $30 deed recording fee and a $20 processing fee are charged for each purchase; card payments carry a 2.75% fee.
answers.quote: There will be a $30 deed recording fee and a $20 processing fee for each purchase. Credit Card (with 2.75% Credit Card Fees applied), Cashiers Check and Wire Transfers are the only acceptable payments.

answers.source_title: Surplus Properties - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.answer: The buyer must not directly or indirectly hold more than a de minimis legal interest in any property with delinquent property taxes in the same county.
answers.quote: The person does not directly or indirectly hold more than a de minimis legal interest in any property with delinquent property taxes located in the same county as the property.

answers.source_title: Surplus Properties - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
answers.note: Same page: 'Credit Card (with 2.75% Credit Card Fees applied), Cashiers Check and Wire Transfers are the only acceptable payments.'

Please perform your due diligence carefully, and be sure you fully understand what you are purchasing.

answers.source_title: Priorities, Policies and Procedures of the Oceana County Land Bank Authority (PDF)
answers.answer: The Land Bank sets the consideration in its sole discretion, considering both fair market value and its property costs (acquisition, maintenance, repair, demolition, marketing and indirect costs).
answers.quote: In each and every transfer of real property the LBA shall require good and valuable consideration in an amount determined by the LBA in its sole discretion. The LBA will consider both the fair market value of the property and the Property Costs in its determination of the consideration for each property.

answers.answer: The buyer is given a quit claim deed; all property is sold as is.

answers.source_title: Priorities, Policies and Procedures of the Oceana County Land Bank Authority
answers.answer: For property rehabilitated by the Land Bank, a nonrefundable escrow deposit is required, not less than $500 for a purchase price under $30,000 and $1000 above $30,000.

AUCTIONS.summary: An online auction of tax-forfeited land the county holds (Wright County).

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.note: Section added by 2024 c 127 art 70 s 4.
answers.answer: Before managing tax-forfeited land any other way, the county must first offer forfeited parcels at a public auction run by the county auditor and sell to the highest bidder.
answers.quote: Prior to managing tax-forfeited lands as otherwise provided in this chapter, a county must first offer tax-forfeited parcels for sale pursuant to this section ... The county auditor must sell the property at a public auction to the highest bidder in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: The sale must occur within six months of the filing of the certificate of forfeiture or the date the property is vacated, whichever is later, with notice published at least 30 days before the sale starts.
answers.quote: The sale under this section must occur within six months of either the filing of the certificate of forfeiture pursuant to section 281.23, subdivision 9 , or the date the property is vacated by the occupant, whichever is later. Notice of the sale under this subdivision must be provided by publication in newspapers, websites, and other forums that serve diverse communities in the county where the property is located at least 30 days before the commencement of the sale.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: The law allows the public auction to be held online; a county may also sell tax-forfeited lands through an online auction with posted and website notice at least ten days before it begins.
answers.quote: in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction. ... may sell tax-forfeited lands through an online auction. When an online auction is used to sell tax-forfeited lands, the county auditor shall post a physical notice of the online auction and shall publish a notice of the online auction on its website not less than ten days before the online auction begins

answers.where_to_look: See Minn. Stat. 282.005, subd. 4 (public auction 'in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction'). The statute sets no bidder-registration procedure. Each county or its auction platform does - Ramsey uses the State's MNBid site, Hubbard needs no pre-registration, see the county answers.

links.title: Minn. Stat. 282.005, subd. 4 (public auction 'in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction')

answers.where_to_look: See Minn. Stat. 282.005, subd. 4-5 (public auction; sale proceeds). The statute sets no bidder deposit. Ramsey's online-sale terms require none either - the winning bid is paid in full after the award.

links.title: Minn. Stat. 282.005, subd. 4-5 (public auction; sale proceeds)

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: The starting price is the estimated market value from the most recent assessment, and the property may not sell below it for 30 days. If no buyer pays it, the price drops to the minimum bid: the delinquent taxes, special assessments, penalties, interest and costs.
answers.quote: "minimum bid" means the sum of delinquent taxes, special assessments, penalties, interests, and costs assigned to the parcel. ... the initial price of the property, which is equal to the estimated market value, as determined by the most recent assessment. The property must not be sold for less than the initial price for 30 days after it is initially made available at auction. If no buyer is willing to pay the initial price, the price for the property must be reduced to the minimum bid.

answers.source_title: Sec. 282.01 MN Statutes
answers.note: The statute sets no payment deadline; the county's sale terms do (see the Ramsey and Hubbard rows).
answers.answer: Parcels are sold for cash only unless the county board has adopted a resolution for sale on terms; on terms, at least ten percent of the purchase price is paid at the time of purchase and the balance in no more than ten equal annual installments, or per county board policy.
answers.quote: The parcels must be sold for cash only, unless the county board of the county has adopted a resolution providing for their sale on terms, in which event the resolution controls with respect to the sale. When the sale is made on terms other than for cash only (1) a payment of at least ten percent of the purchase price must be made at the time of purchase, and the balance must be paid in no more than ten equal annual installments, or (2) the payments must be made in accordance with county board policy

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: A $25 fee is collected in addition to the sale price when the land is fully paid for.
answers.quote: and upon full payment for the land, plus a $25 fee in addition to the sale price, the sale shall be complete and a conveyance of the land shall be issued to the purchaser

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: After full payment, a conveyance is issued to the purchaser according to the land's status on forfeiture. Any conveyance of forfeited land reserves all minerals and mineral rights to the state.
answers.quote: a conveyance of the land shall be issued to the purchaser as provided by the appropriate statutes according to the status of the land upon forfeiture. ... Any conveyance of forfeited lands shall be subject to exceptions and reservations in this state, in trust for the taxing districts of all minerals and mineral rights.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: The law provides for repurchase by an interested party before the public sale, by paying all delinquent taxes and assessments with penalties, interest and costs.
answers.quote: Prior to the public sale required under this section, an interested party may repurchase the property by payment of the sum of all delinquent taxes and assessments computed under section 282.251 , together with penalties, interest, and costs, that accrued or would have accrued if the parcel of land had not forfeited.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: Forfeiture extinguishes all liens, claims and encumbrances except: interested parties' rights to surplus proceeds, redemption rights under federal law, easements and rights-of-way of holders who are not interested parties, and recorded real covenants.
answers.quote: The forfeiture of the property extinguishes all liens, claims, and encumbrances other than: (1) the rights of interested parties to surplus proceeds under this section; (2) rights of redemption provided under federal law; (3) easements and rights-of-way holders who are not interested parties; and (4) benefits or burdens of any real covenants filed of record as of the date of forfeiture.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: If no buyer pays the minimum bid, the state is deemed to have bought the property by a credit bid, and the parcel may be disposed of under the rest of chapter 282.
answers.quote: If no buyer is willing to pay the minimum bid, the state is deemed to have purchased the property through a credit bid and the parcels may be disposed of as otherwise provided in this chapter.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: Proceeds above the minimum bid are available to interested parties. Within 60 days of the sale the county auditor must notify them of the surplus with a claim form, and they may claim it if they file within six months from the date the notice is first mailed.
answers.quote: The proceeds in excess of the minimum bid shall be available for distribution pursuant to subdivision 6. ... If a sale under this section results in a surplus, within 60 days of the sale, the county auditor must notify interested parties, in a manner described in subdivision 7, of the surplus by sending notice of the surplus and a claim form to the interested parties. ... Interested parties are entitled to make a claim for surplus proceeds under this subdivision if they file a claim within six months from the date the notice is first mailed to the interested parties.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: After all parcels in a county sale have been offered to the highest bidder, the county auditor sells any remaining parcels to anyone offering the appraised value.
answers.quote: and shall sell them to the highest bidder, but not for a sum less than the appraised value, until all of the parcels of land have been offered. Then the county auditor shall sell any remaining parcels to anyone offering to pay the appraised value

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: Remaining parcels are sold by the county auditor to anyone offering to pay the appraised value. A person who could have repurchased the parcel may not buy it for less than all taxes, assessments, penalties, interest and costs due at forfeiture.
answers.quote: Then the county auditor shall sell any remaining parcels to anyone offering to pay the appraised value, except that if the person could have repurchased a parcel of property under section 282.012 or 282.241 , that person may not purchase that same parcel of property at the sale under this subdivision for a purchase price less than the sum of all taxes, assessments, penalties, interest, and costs due at the time of forfeiture

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: Parcels are appraised by the county board, and the sale may not be for less than the appraised value, except under the city-sale alternate procedure.
answers.quote: Any parcels of land proposed to be sold shall be first appraised by the county board of the county in which the parcels lie. ... The sale must not be for less than the appraised value except as provided in subdivision 7a.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: A $25 fee is collected in addition to the sale price on full payment.
answers.quote: and upon full payment for the land, plus a $25 fee in addition to the sale price, the sale shall be complete

answers.answer: After full payment, a conveyance is issued according to the land's status on forfeiture; all minerals and mineral rights are reserved to the state.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: The sale continues until all parcels are sold or until the county board orders a reappraisal or withdraws parcels from sale.
answers.quote: The sale must continue until all the parcels are sold or until the county board orders a reappraisal or withdraws any or all of the parcels from sale.

answers.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
answers.answer: No sale frees a parcel from the lien for the special benefit of a public improvement made after forfeiture until the cost of that improvement, including any penalties, is paid.
answers.quote: No sale of a parcel of land shall discharge or free the parcel of land from lien for the special benefit conferred upon it by reason of the public improvement until the cost of it, including penalties, if any, is paid.

AUCTIONS.summary: A county or city tax sale of the property (not tracked).

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.150 RSMo
answers.note: Missouri ch. 140 is the general county tax sale law; St. Louis City and Jackson County collect delinquent land taxes under other chapters (ch. 92 / ch. 141), not read for these statewide rows.
answers.answer: Land on which taxes or special assessments are delinquent is subject to sale to discharge the tax lien, held on the fourth Monday in August each year.
answers.quote: All lands, lots, mineral rights, and royalty interests on which taxes or special assessments are delinquent and unpaid are subject to sale to discharge the lien for the delinquent and unpaid taxes or unpaid special assessments as provided for in this chapter on the fourth Monday in August of each year.

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.170 RSMo
answers.note: Missouri ch. 140 is the general county tax sale law; St. Louis City and Jackson County collect delinquent land taxes under other chapters (ch. 92 / ch. 141), not read for these statewide rows.
answers.answer: The sale is held in or next to the courthouse on the fourth Monday in August, starting at ten o'clock and continuing from day to day until all land is offered.
answers.quote: will be sold at public auction to discharge the taxes, penalty, interest, and costs due thereon at the time of sale in or adjacent to the courthouse of such county, on the fourth Monday in August next thereafter, commencing at ten o'clock of said day and continuing from day to day thereafter until all are offered.

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.170 RSMo
answers.answer: The auction is held in or next to the county courthouse; the collector may also run it at the same time by electronic media, including the internet.
answers.quote: in or adjacent to the courthouse of such county ... Such auction may also be conducted by electronic media, including the internet, at the same time and at the discretion of the county collector.

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.190 RSMo
answers.answer: No sale is made to a person who is currently delinquent on taxes on other property and does not sign an affidavit stating such at the time of sale. A nonresident must file a written consent to the jurisdiction of the county's circuit court.
answers.quote: no sale shall be made to any person or designated agent who: (a) Is currently delinquent on any tax payments on any property, other than a delinquency on the property being offered for sale, and who does not sign an affidavit stating such at the time of sale. ... A nonresident shall file with said collector an agreement in writing consenting to the jurisdiction of the circuit court of the county in which such sale shall be made

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.190 RSMo
answers.note: No statutory deposit requirement was found in ch. 140; check the county collector.
answers.where_to_look: See Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.190 RSMo.

links.title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.190 RSMo

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.240 RSMo
answers.answer: At the first offering, if no one bids a sum equal to the delinquent taxes with interest, penalty and costs, the land is not sold and is offered again at the next sale.
answers.quote: If at the first offering of sale of any tract of land or lot under the provisions of this law, no person bids therefor a sum equal to the delinquent taxes thereon with interest, penalty and costs

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.280 RSMo
answers.answer: The purchaser must pay the bid to the collector immediately. A purchaser who fails to pay forfeits a penalty of twenty-five percent of the bid, and the land is offered again.
answers.quote: the purchaser at such sale shall immediately pay the amount of his bid to the collector ... In case the purchaser fails to pay his bid, the land shall be again forthwith offered for sale the same as if no sale had been made, and the purchaser so failing shall forfeit and pay for the use of the distributive county school fund of the county a penalty of twenty-five percent of the amount of his bid

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.290 RSMo
answers.answer: For each certificate of purchase, the purchaser pays the collector the fee to record the certificate with the county recorder, as part of the cost of the sale.
answers.quote: For each certificate of purchase issued, as a part of the cost of the sale, the purchaser shall pay to the collector the fee necessary to record such certificate of purchase in the office of the county recorder.

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.420 RSMo
answers.answer: The collector executes a deed in the name of the state that vests an absolute estate in fee simple, subject to claims for unpaid taxes (other than certain inferior ones).
answers.quote: The collector of the county in which the sale of such lands took place shall execute to the purchaser or the purchaser's heirs or assigns, in the name of the state, a conveyance of the real estate so sold, which shall vest in the grantee an absolute estate in fee simple, subject, however, to all claims thereon for unpaid taxes

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.340 RSMo
answers.note: Third offering: RSMo 140.250.1 (ninety-day redemption); post-third-offering sales: RSMo 140.250.4 (no period of redemption).
answers.answer: The owner, lienholder, occupant or others with an interest have an absolute right to redeem for one year after the sale, and a defeasible right until the purchaser acquires the deed.
answers.quote: shall have the absolute right to redeem the same at any time during the one year next ensuing and shall continue to have a defeasible right to redeem the same until such time as the tax sale purchaser acquires the deed

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.420 RSMo
answers.answer: The deed is subject to claims for unpaid taxes, except unpaid taxes whose lien was inferior to the lien for which the land was sold.
answers.quote: subject, however, to all claims thereon for unpaid taxes except such unpaid taxes, existing at time of the purchase of said lands and the lien for which taxes was inferior to the lien for taxes for which said tract or lot of land was sold

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.250 RSMo
answers.answer: If land is not sold at the third offering, the collector advertises or offers it for sale once every thirty days.
answers.quote: If any lands or lots are not sold at such third offering, then the collector shall advertise or offer such lands or lots for sale once every thirty days.

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.405 RSMo
answers.answer: The purchaser must obtain a title search report from a licensed attorney or licensed title company detailing the ownership and encumbrances on the property.
answers.quote: The purchaser shall obtain a title search report from a licensed attorney or licensed title company detailing the ownership and encumbrances on the property.

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 141.980 RSMo
answers.note: St. Louis City's Land Reutilization Authority is created under RSMo 92.875 instead (see the St. Louis City rows).
answers.answer: A municipality in a county operating wholly under the Land Tax Collection Law may establish a land bank agency to manage, sell, transfer and dispose of real estate the agency owns.
answers.quote: Any municipality located wholly or partially within a county electing to operate wholly under the provisions of sections 141.210 to 141.810 may establish a land bank agency for the management, sale, transfer, and other disposition of interests in real estate owned by such land bank agency.

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 141.985 RSMo
answers.note: Chapter 141 Municipal Land Bank Act (RSMo 141.980 to 141.1015). St. Louis City's Land Reutilization Authority operates under RSMo 92.875 instead.
answers.answer: A land bank agency must accept written offers equal to or greater than fair market value. If it rejects such an offer or does not respond within sixty days, its action is subject to judicial review unless it accepted another such offer.
answers.quote: A land bank agency shall accept written offers equal to or greater than fair market value to purchase real property held by the land bank agency. If a land bank agency rejects a written offer equal to or greater than fair market value, or does not respond to a written offer equal to or greater than fair market value within sixty days, the land bank agency's action shall be subject to judicial review

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 141.985 RSMo
answers.answer: Each land bank agency's board sets the general terms and conditions for the consideration it receives for transfers in its policies and procedures.
answers.quote: The land bank agency shall determine and set forth in policies and procedures of the board the general terms and conditions for consideration to be received by the land bank agency for the transfer of real property and interests in real property

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 141.985
answers.note: Chapter 141 Municipal Land Bank Act (Kansas City); the St. Louis Land Reutilization Authority operates under RSMo 92.700 to 92.920, which set no holding period.
answers.answer: A land bank agency's public inventory must show whether each parcel is available for sale and the year it entered the inventory. Where the agency owns more than five parcels in one city block and no written offer has been submitted in the past twelve months, it must reduce its requested price and advertise the discount.
answers.quote: include at a minimum whether a parcel is available for sale, the address of the parcel if an address has been assigned, the parcel number, if no address has been assigned, and the year that a parcel entered the land bank agency's inventory. ... If a land bank agency owns more than five parcels of real property in a single city block and no written offer to purchase any of those properties has been submitted to the agency in the past twelve months, the land bank shall reduce its requested price for those properties and advertise the discount publicly.

answers.source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 141.1009 RSMo
answers.answer: A land bank agency may file an action to quiet title under section 527.150 for any real property in which it has an interest. The court must hold a hearing within ninety days of filing.
answers.quote: A land bank agency shall be authorized to file an action to quiet title pursuant to section 527.150 as to any real property in which the land bank agency has an interest. ... The court shall schedule a hearing on the petition within ninety days following filing of the petition

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Oklahoma repealed its tax certificate sale sections in 2008 (Laws 2008, c. 82); 68 O.S. 3105.1 keeps earlier liens under the old law. Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: When real estate taxes have been unpaid for three years or more, the county treasurer advertises and sells the real estate at the annual tax resale for those taxes and all other delinquent taxes, special assessments and costs.
answers.quote: where taxes are a lien upon real property and have been unpaid for a period of three (3) years or more as of the date such taxes first became due and payable, advertise and sell such real estate for such taxes and all other delinquent taxes, special assessments and costs at the tax resale provided for in

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: The resale is held on the second Monday of June each year; an online resale starts during normal business hours within the full week of the second Monday of June.
answers.quote: the county treasurer shall proceed to sell such real estate at resale, which shall be held on the second Monday of June each year in each county or, if co nducted through an online auction, shall be started on a date and time set by the county treasurer during normal business hours within the full week of the second Monday of June

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: Property must sell for at least two-thirds of its current assessed value or the total taxes, penalties, interest and costs due, whichever is less.
answers.quote: All property must be sold for a sum not less than two-thirds (2/3) of the assessed value of such real estate as fixed for the current fiscal year, or for the total amount of taxes, penalties, interest and costs due on such property, whichever is the l esser.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: Property is sold at public auction to the highest bidder for cash or certified funds; online auctions may accept online payments.
answers.quote: The real estate shall be sold at public auction to the highest bidder for cash or certified funds. Online a uctions may accept online payments.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: In addition to the bid, the treasurer collects enough to pay the county's expenses of preparing, listing and advertising the property.
answers.quote: The county treasurer shall also charge ... an amount in addition to the bid placed on such real estate, sufficient to pay all expenses incurred by the county in preparing, listing and advertising the lot or tract purchased by such bidder

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Surface rights: 68 O.S. 3119. No action to set aside the deed may begin twelve months after it is filed (3131(A)).
answers.answer: The resale deed vests absolute and perfect title in fee simple, subject to all claims the state may have for taxes or other liens or encumbrances.
answers.quote: shall vest in the grantee an absolute and perfect title in fee simple to the real estate, subject to all claims which the state may have had on the real estate for taxes or other liens or encumbrances

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Disability exception also in 68 O.S. 3131(A).
answers.answer: The owner or anyone with a legal or equitable interest may redeem only before the resale auction starts, by paying the original delinquency with interest and costs.
answers.quote: may redeem the same at any time before the start of the resale auction by paying to the county treasurer the sum which was originally delinquent including interest at the lawful rate

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: State claims: 68 O.S. 3131(A); covenants: 68 O.S. 3145.
answers.answer: The resale tax deed does not extinguish the mortgage of a mortgagee to whom no notice was sent.
answers.quote: the resale tax deed shall be ineffective to extinguish any mortgage on said real estate of a mortgagee to whom no notice was sent.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.answer: If no bid reaches the required minimum, the county treasurer bids the property off in the name of the county.
answers.quote: if there is no bid equal to or greater than the sum so required, the county treasurer shall bid off the same in the name of the county.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

answers.quote: Using the information provided, the OHCA shall produce a list for each county of properties on which the OHCA has liens. The coun ty treasurers shall make the list of properties with the OHCA liens available to potential buyers at the tax resales.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

answers.answer: Property the county acquired at the tax resale may be sold by the county treasurer after notice by publication, at a price approved by the board of county commissioners.
answers.quote: Any property acquired by the county under the provisions of the resale tax laws may be sold by the county treasurer, after notice by publication, at a price as may be approved by the board of county commissioners, the notice to be given after receipt o f bid on the property.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: On the date in the published notice, the property is sold to the highest competitive bidder for cash in hand or certified funds, or to the original bidder if no higher price is offered, subject to the board of county commissioners' approval.
answers.quote: On the date stated in the notice, the property shall be sold by the county treasurer to the hig hest competitive bidder, for cash in hand or certified funds , or to the original bidder if there be no higher price offered. The sale in any event shall be subject to the approval of the board of county commissioners in its discretion.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: At a county auction, a bid below all the ad valorem taxes owed at the original resale is accepted only with the approval of the county commissioners and the county excise board.
answers.quote: Any bid which is less than all of the real estate ad valorem taxes owed at the time of the original resale shall be accepted only upon approval of the county commissioners and the coun ty excise board.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: Advertising and other sale expenses are added to the sale price as a separate charge paid by the purchaser in addition to the bid; a bidder must deposit enough to cover the advertisement and costs before the property is advertised, and the recording cost is part of the cost of sale paid by the purchaser.
answers.quote: shall be apportioned to the respective tracts listed in the sale and shall be added to the sale price of the real estate as a separate and additional charge and shall be paid by the purc haser, in addition to the amount bid upon the real estate. A deposit shall be required of any bidder before advertisement of the property to cover the advertisement and costs. ... The cost of recording shall be considered a part of the cost of sale, and shall be paid by the purchaser.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
