answers.quote: The State Auditor and Inspector shall p rescribe, for the use of the several county treasurers, a form of bid and form of report of sale.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.answer: Bidders must pay a deposit before the property is advertised to cover advertising and costs.
answers.quote: A deposit shall be required of any bidder before advertisement of the property to cover the advertisement and costs.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: After the commissioners approve the sale, their chair executes a deed conveying title on a form prescribed by the State Auditor and Inspector.
answers.quote: Upon approval of the sale as hereinbefore provided, the chair of the board of county commissioners shall execute a deed conveying title to the purchaser of the property in as full and ample manner as by law provide d on a form prescribed by the State Auditor and Inspector.

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: The statute sets no period after which county-held property leaves the list. Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: The county holds property it acquired at resale until it is sold; a sale follows a notice the treasurer publishes once during each of the three consecutive weeks preceding the sale.
answers.quote: Any property acquired by the county under the provisions of the resale tax laws may be sold by the county treasurer, after notice by publication ... The notice shall be published by the county treasurer once during each of the three (3) consecutive weeks preceding the sale

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.note: The first two pieces are the resale deed's effect (3131(A)), including the proviso for property bid off to the county; the third is 3145 (covenants in a city or town). Quote copied as the Legislature's RTF renders to text: the file hard-wraps lines inside words, so a few words carry a stray space (e.g. 'coun ty'); the wording is the statute's.
answers.answer: The resale deed vests an absolute fee simple title subject to claims the state may have had on the real estate for taxes or other liens or encumbrances; where the property was bid off in the name of the county, those claims are canceled and extinguished. Recorded restrictions and covenants running with the land survive a resale tax deed.
answers.quote: shall vest in the grantee an absolute and perfect title in fee simple to the real estate, subject to all claims which the state may have had on the real estate for taxes or other liens or encumbrances ... shall be canceled and extinguished with respect to any deed conveying title to the board of county commissioners where such property was bid off in the name of the county ... said restrictions and covenants shall survive and be enforceable after the issuance of a resale or certificate tax deed

answers.source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
answers.answer: The county's resale property fund reimburses a purchaser at resale or at commissioners' sale where no tax was due or the sale was illegal and the purchaser has no adequate recourse against the property. A refund claim not filed within three (3) years from the sale is not paid.
answers.quote: For the reimbursement of the purchaser at resale or at commissioners' sale of any lot, tract, or parcel of real estate, sold at resale, against which no tax was due ... or where the sale thereof to such purchaser was illegal for any other reason; and such purchaser has no adequate recourse against the property thus sold ... Provided, however, that no claim for refund not filed, as herein provided, within a period of three (3) years from the date of such sale shall be allowed or paid from said fund

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 626 (72 P.S. 5860.626)
answers.note: Land banks (68 Pa.C.S. Ch. 21) are a separate program: a land bank must keep a public inventory of its property (68 Pa.C.S. 2110(a)).
answers.answer: Property that remains unsold after being exposed to a judicial sale is placed in a "repository for unsold properties". The county tax claim bureau keeps the list and makes it available to the public during normal office hours.
answers.quote: If, after conducting and exposing a property to a judicial sale under the provisions of this act, whether prior to, at the time of or after the effective date of this amendatory act, any property remains unsold, it shall be placed in a category to be termed "repository for unsold properties." A list of properties in this category shall be maintained by the bureau and shall be available during normal office hours to the general public.

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(a) (72 P.S. 5860.627)
answers.answer: With the written consent of all taxing districts, the bureau may set a minimum purchase price and accept an offer at or above it without court approval. A taxing district may require the buyer to appear in person before its governing body.
answers.quote: The bureau may, with the written consent of all the taxing districts where the property is located, establish a minimum purchase price and accept an offer of any price equal to or greater than the minimum purchase price for property placed in the "repository for unsold properties" without court approval and published notice of sale.

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(a) (72 P.S. 5860.627)
answers.note: Land bank part from 68 Pa.C.S. 2110(c)(1): "A land bank shall determine the amount and form of consideration necessary to convey, exchange, sell, transfer, lease as lessor, grant or mortgage interests in real property." (https://www.palegis.us/statutes/consolidated/view-statute?txtType=HTM&ttl=68&div=0&chapter=21&section=10&subsctn=0, read 2026-10-29)
answers.answer: For repository property, the bureau may set a minimum purchase price with the written consent of all taxing districts and accept an offer at or above it.
answers.quote: establish a minimum purchase price and accept an offer of any price equal to or greater than the minimum purchase price

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(b), 631(b)
answers.answer: The bureau records the deed at the purchaser's expense. A county that has adopted the ordinance may also collect a fee of up to $250 from the buyer at the time of sale for its demolition and rehabilitation fund.
answers.quote: It shall be the responsibility of the bureau to have the deed recorded at the expense of the purchaser. ... The governing body of a county may, by ordinance, impose a fee not to exceed two hundred fifty dollars ($250) for the sale of any property being sold in accordance with this act

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(a), 502-A
answers.answer: The purchaser must give an affidavit with the information in section 502-A, including a statement that the purchaser is not delinquent in real estate taxes to any taxing district in Pennsylvania.
answers.quote: The bureau shall require, as a condition of sale, that the purchaser provide an affidavit that includes the information specified under section 502-A. ... is not delinquent in paying real estate taxes to any taxing district in this Commonwealth

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(b)
answers.answer: The property is conveyed upon payment of the agreed price.
answers.quote: The property shall be conveyed to the purchaser upon payment of the agreed price

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(b)
answers.answer: Repository property is conveyed free and clear of all tax and municipal claims, mortgages, liens, charges and estates of any kind, except ground rents separately taxed.
answers.quote: The property shall be conveyed to the purchaser upon payment of the agreed price, free and clear of all tax and municipal claims, mortgages, liens, and charges and estates of whatsoever kind, except ground rents separately taxed.

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.answer: Property that remains unsold after a judicial sale is placed in the repository for unsold properties, and the bureau keeps the list available to the public during normal office hours; the bureau may accept an offer at or above the minimum purchase price without court approval or published notice. The quoted sections set no time limit.
answers.quote: any property remains unsold, it shall be placed in a category to be termed "repository for unsold properties." A list of properties in this category shall be maintained by the bureau and shall be available during normal office hours to the general public. ... The bureau may, with the written consent of all the taxing districts where the property is located, establish a minimum purchase price and accept an offer of any price equal to or greater than the minimum purchase price for property placed in the "repository for unsold properties" without court approval and published notice of sale.

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.answer: Repository property is conveyed on payment of the agreed price free and clear of all tax and municipal claims, mortgages, liens, charges and estates, except ground rents separately taxed. The deed is recorded at the purchaser's expense.
answers.quote: The property shall be conveyed to the purchaser upon payment of the agreed price, free and clear of all tax and municipal claims, mortgages, liens, and charges and estates of whatsoever kind, except ground rents separately taxed. It shall be the responsibility of the bureau to have the deed recorded at the expense of the purchaser.

answers.source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
answers.note: No statewide buyer due-diligence statement found in the Act; see the Fayette county row.
answers.where_to_look: See Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly).

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.summary: A tax lien or certificate (not tracked).

answers.source_title: Real Estate - Pittsburgh, PA
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: The Real Estate Division of the City of Pittsburgh Department of Finance handles purchases of city-owned property; phone 412-255-2300.
answers.quote: For additional information about the vacant lots, call the Real Estate Division at: 412-255-2300 The Real Estate Division of the Department of Finance accepts questions from the general public for purchase of properties.

answers.source_title: Real Estate - Pittsburgh, PA
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: Buyers submit a Request to Purchase through the city's online portal with a $25 application fee per property; the city checks that the applicant is a qualified buyer (taxes, water and sewage paid, in compliance with city codes and policies) and tells the approved purchaser the price in its response letter.
answers.quote: all Request to Purchase applications must be submitted through our online portal ... A $25 application fee per property will apply. ... The prospective purchaser submits a request to become a qualified buyer. A qualified buyer is one who: Has paid taxes, water, sewage, etc. Is in compliance with City codes and policies. The approved prospective purchaser is notified of the price in the response letter to the Request to Purchase form.

answers.source_title: Real Estate - Pittsburgh, PA
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: Prices online show TBD; a property is priced after the applicant is approved as a buyer, and the approved purchaser is told the price in the response letter to the Request to Purchase form.
answers.quote: The approved prospective purchaser is notified of the price in the response letter to the Request to Purchase form. ... Why do the prices online all say “TBD?” Pricing of all properties will be done after you are approved as a buyer.

answers.source_title: Procedures for Purchasing Property Through Standard Court Auction Sales (City of Pittsburgh Department of Finance, rev. 9.30.25)
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: A non-refundable $25.00 per parcel application fee; the purchaser pays for the insurable title report; the buyer pays all related costs, and the deed is recorded immediately upon closing.
answers.quote: A non refundable $25.00 per parcel application fee will apply. ... The report must be paid for by the purchaser, and may or may not include title insurance. ... The buyer must pay all related costs and the deed must be recorded immediately upon closing.

answers.source_title: Real Estate - Pittsburgh, PA
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: A Request to Purchase application submitted through the city's online portal, one property per form; paper and e-mailed applications are not accepted.
answers.quote: all Request to Purchase applications must be submitted through our online portal ... Paper applications and applications sent via email will no longer be accepted. ... There can only be one piece of property requested per form. If you are requesting multiple properties, each piece will require a new, separate, Request to Purchase form.

answers.source_title: Procedures for Purchasing Property Through Standard Court Auction Sales (City of Pittsburgh Department of Finance, rev. 9.30.25)
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: After approval the buyer places a 10% non-refundable deposit (minimum $200.00) by cashier's check or money order payable to the Director of Finance; the remaining balance is paid at closing, by cashier's check or money order, within sixty (60) days of the notice that the deed is ready.
answers.quote: The prospective buyer must place a 10% non- refundable deposit (minimum $200.00) with the Real Estate Division. The deposit must be in the form of a cashier’s check or money order made payable to the Director of Finance. ... The buyer will be required to close and pay the remaining balance within sixty (60) days of the notification. Final settlement of the sale must be paid by cashier’s check or money order.

answers.source_title: Procedures for Purchasing Property Through Standard Court Auction Sales (City of Pittsburgh Department of Finance, rev. 9.30.25)
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: A quit claim deed prepared by City Law and signed by the Mayor after a final Order of Court confirms the sale.
answers.quote: A final Order of Court will confirm the sale to the buyer or successful bidder. City Law will prepare and execute a deed that will be signed by the Mayor. ... Title will be conveyed by quit claim deed.

answers.source_title: Procedures for Purchasing Property Through Standard Court Auction Sales (City of Pittsburgh Department of Finance, rev. 9.30.25)
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: The city's procedure says the sale process may take 12 – 18 months or longer and that ownership may not be guaranteed; it does not say how long a property stays listed.
answers.quote: THESE PROCEDURES MAY TAKE 12 – 18 MONTHS OR LONGER, AND OWNERSHIP MAY NOT BE GUARANTEED

answers.source_title: Real Estate - Pittsburgh, PA
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: The city says the title and property are free and clear of all back taxes and liens when the buyer closes.
answers.quote: Will I get the properties purchased from the City of Pittsburgh with a clear title? Yes. The title and property will be free and clear of all back taxes and liens when you close on the property.

answers.source_title: Procedures for Purchasing Property Through Standard Court Auction Sales (City of Pittsburgh Department of Finance, rev. 9.30.25)
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: After Council approval the buyer orders and pays for an insurable title report, which may or may not include title insurance; the Law Department uses it to petition the Court of Common Pleas to validate the title, and title is conveyed by quit claim deed.
answers.quote: After Council approval is received, the City will notify the buyer in writing to order an insurable title report. The report must be paid for by the purchaser, and may or may not include title insurance. ... The Law Department will use the Title Report to prepare and submit a petition for a Rule to Show Cause to the Court of Common Pleas authorizing and validating the title. ... Title will be conveyed by quit claim deed.

answers.source_title: Real Estate - Pittsburgh, PA
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: Not before approval; once approved and sent a correspondence letter, the buyer can set a date and time to view the property.
answers.quote: Can I view the property/properties that I requested before I am approved? No. You will be able to set a date and time to view the property once you have been approved and received a correspondence letter from the City.

answers.source_title: Procedures for Purchasing Property Through Standard Court Auction Sales (City of Pittsburgh Department of Finance, rev. 9.30.25)
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: The 10% deposit (minimum $200.00) is non-refundable and hand money is forfeited if the buyer does not comply with the procedures; hand money is refunded if City Council denies the sale.
answers.quote: The prospective buyer must place a 10% non- refundable deposit (minimum $200.00) with the Real Estate Division. ... If denied by Council, hand money will be refunded. ... FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH THESE PROCEDURES WILL RESULT IN THE CANCELLATION OF THE SALE AND FORFEITURE OF HAND MONEY.

answers.source_title: Procedures for Purchasing Property Through Standard Court Auction Sales (City of Pittsburgh Department of Finance, rev. 9.30.25)
answers.office: Real Estate Division, Department of Finance, City of Pittsburgh
answers.answer: The city warns that failure to comply with its procedures cancels the sale and forfeits the hand money, that the procedures may take 12 – 18 months or longer, and that ownership may not be guaranteed.
answers.quote: FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH THESE PROCEDURES WILL RESULT IN THE CANCELLATION OF THE SALE AND FORFEITURE OF HAND MONEY. THESE PROCEDURES MAY TAKE 12 – 18 MONTHS OR LONGER, AND OWNERSHIP MAY NOT BE GUARANTEED

answers.source_title: Tax Sale Information | Fayette County, PA
answers.answer: Fayette County Tax Claim Bureau, 2 West Main Street, Uniontown PA 15401; phone 724-430-1208; Monday - Friday 8 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.
answers.quote: Tax Claim Bureau 2 West Main Street Uniontown PA 15401 Directions Phone 724-430-1208 Fax 724-491-2928 Hours Monday - Friday 8 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.

answers.source_title: Tax Sale Information | Fayette County, PA
answers.answer: Repository properties can be bid on at any time by sealed bid. Bids are opened on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 a.m.; the municipality and school district accept or reject the bid, and the bureau notifies by mail within 30-45 days.
answers.quote: If the property still does not sell, it is put on our Repository List and can be bid on at any time. We keep the sealed bids in a lockbox. We open the envelopes on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 a.m. It is the decision of the authorities to accept or reject your bid. (Municipality and School District) We will notify you by mail within 30-45 days of the decision.

answers.source_title: Fayette County Tax Claim Bureau - Repository Sale Sealed Bid Form
answers.answer: The bureau's checklist: one bid form, the Affidavit of Bidder(s), a money order, certified check or cashier's check for the bid amount, in an envelope marked "Sealed Repository Bid".
answers.quote: CHECK LIST: ... ONE BID FORM ... AFFIDAVIT OF BIDDER(S) ... MONEY ORDER, CERTIFIED CHECK, OR CASHIER'S CHECK FOR BID AMOUNT ... ENVELOPE MARKED SEALED REPOSITORY BID

answers.source_title: Fayette County Tax Claim Bureau - Repository Sale Sealed Bid Form
answers.answer: Enclose a money order, certified check or cashier's check for the bid amount with the sealed bid.
answers.quote: MONEY ORDER, CERTIFIED ... CHECK, OR CASHIER'S CHECK ... FOR BID AMOUNT

answers.source_title: Fayette County, PA - Tax Claim Bureau
answers.answer: Property that does not sell goes on the Repository List and can be bid on at any time. Sealed bids are opened on the first Tuesday of the month, bidders are notified by mail within 30-45 days of the decision, and recording the deed may take up to six months.
answers.quote: If the property still does not sell, it is put on our Repository List and can be bid on at any time. ... We open the envelopes on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 a.m. ... We will notify you by mail within 30-45 days of the decision. Deeds are typed in our office; it may take up to six months to have them recorded.

answers.source_title: Tax Claim Bureau - Affidavit of Repository Bidder (Fayette County, PA)
answers.answer: Properties are offered without any guarantee or warranty as to the record title or otherwise, and no adjustments are made after the bureau accepts a bid.
answers.quote: ALL PROPERTIES ARE OFFERED FOR SALE WITHOUT ANY GUARANTEE OR WARRANTY WHATSOEVER, AS TO THE RECORD TITLE OR OTHERWISE, AND NO ADJUSTMENTS OF ANY KIND WILL BE MADE AFTER THE TAX CLAIM BUREAU HAS ACCEPTED YOUR BID.

answers.source_title: Tax Claim Bureau - Affidavit of Repository Bidder (Fayette County, PA)
answers.answer: The bureau's affidavit tells bidders to conduct their own inspection of the title before placing a bid, because the bureau does not guarantee that the property is not slated for demolition or condemnation; it does not address physical inspection of the property.
answers.quote: ALSO BE ADVISED THAT THE TAX CLAIM BUREAU DOES NOT GUARANTEE THAT THIS PROPERTY HAS NOT BEEN SLATED FOR DEMOLITION OR CONDEMNATION. FOR THAT REASON, BE ADVISED THAT IT WOULD BE PRUDENT TO CONDUCT YOUR OWN INSPECTION OF THE TITLE TO THE PROPERTY YOU ARE PURCHACING PRIOR TO PLACING YOUR BID.

answers.source_title: Tax Claim Bureau - Affidavit of Repository Bidder (Fayette County, PA)
answers.answer: All sales are final and there are no refunds; a bidder found delinquent in taxes or municipal utility bills in Fayette County may not receive a deed and forfeits the bid price.
answers.quote: SHOULD WE DISCOVER THAT YOU ARE DELINQUENT IN TAXES OR MUNICIPAL UTILITY BILLS ON ANY PROPERTY IN FAYETTE COUNTY, YOU MAY NOT RECEIVE A DEED TO THE PROPERTY ON WHICH YOU BID AND YOU WILL FORFEIT YOUR BID PRICE. I UNDERSTAND AND ACKNOWLEDGE THAT ALL SALES ARE FINAL. THERE ARE NO REFUNDS.

answers.source_title: Fayette County, PA - Tax Claim Bureau
answers.answer: The Tax Claim Bureau strongly suggests consulting an attorney before purchasing at any of its sales and states it offers no warranty or guarantee at any sale it conducts.
answers.quote: We, The Tax Claim Bureau offer no warranty or guarantee whatsoever at any sale we conduct. ... It is strongly suggested that you consult with an attorney if you purchase any properties at our sales.

AUCTIONS.summary: A county tax sale of the property, subject to the former owner's redemption period.

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: Real estate whose property taxes are delinquent is advertised and sold at public auction by the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes. The advertisement is titled "Delinquent Tax Sale".
answers.quote: The property duly advertised must be sold, by the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes, at public auction at the courthouse or other convenient place within the county ... The property must be advertised for sale at public auction. The advertisement must be in a newspaper of general circulation within the county or municipality, if applicable, and must be entitled "Delinquent Tax Sale".

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: The sale is held on the advertised date. Real property must be advertised once a week for three consecutive weeks before the legal sales date.
answers.quote: on the advertised date for legal tender payable in full ... The advertising must be published once a week before the legal sales date for three consecutive weeks for the sale of real property

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: The law requires a public auction at the courthouse or at another convenient place within the county, if that place is designated and advertised.
answers.quote: at public auction at the courthouse or other convenient place within the county, if designated and advertised, on the advertised date

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.note: Chapter 51 sets no statewide bidder-registration rule that was found; registration is set by each county (see county rows).
answers.where_to_look: See Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws).

links.title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.note: Chapter 51 requires the full bid on the day of the sale (see payment_deadline); no separate deposit rule was found.
answers.where_to_look: See Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws).

links.title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: The officer conducting the sale submits a bid on behalf of the forfeited land commission equal to all unpaid property taxes, penalties, assessments and costs, including the taxes levied for the year in which the redemption period begins.
answers.quote: shall submit a bid on behalf of the forfeited land commission equal to the amount of all unpaid property taxes, penalties, assessments including, but not limited to, assessments owed to a special taxing district established pursuant to Section 4-9-30, Chapter 19, Title 4, or an assessment district established pursuant to Chapter 15, Title 6, and costs including taxes levied for the year in which the redemption period begins.

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: The successful bidder must pay the full amount of the bid on the day of the sale, in cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order. A bidder who fails to pay has the bid cancelled and is liable for up to five hundred dollars in damages.
answers.quote: for legal tender payable in full by cash, cashier's check, certified check, or money order on the date of the sale. ... The successful bidder at the delinquent tax sale shall pay legal tender as provided in Section 12-51-50 to the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes in the full amount of the bid on the day of the sale. ... The defaulting bidder is liable for no more than five hundred dollars damages upon default

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: If the property is not redeemed, the purchaser pays the actual cost of preparing the tax title plus the documentary stamps and recording fees before the tax title is delivered for recording.
answers.quote: The successful purchaser, or assignee, is responsible for the actual cost of preparing the tax title plus documentary stamps necessary to be affixed and recording fees.

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: If the property is not redeemed, the collector makes a tax title to the purchaser. The tax deed is prima facie evidence of good title, and after a further twelve months it is incontestable on procedural or other grounds.
answers.quote: shall make a tax title to the purchaser or the purchaser's assignee. ... the tax deed issued is incontestable on procedural or other grounds. ... the deed of conveyance, whether executed to a private person, a corporation, or a forfeited land commission, is prima facie evidence of a good title in the holder

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: Yes. The defaulting taxpayer, a grantee from the owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem within twelve months from the date of the sale. Interest on the bid runs from three percent (first three months) to twelve percent (last three months) and may not exceed the forfeited land commission's bid.
answers.quote: The defaulting taxpayer, any grantee from the owner, or any mortgage or judgment creditor may within twelve months from the date of the delinquent tax sale redeem each item of real estate ... First three months three percent of the bid amount ... Last three months twelve percent of the bid amount However, in every redemption, the amount of interest due must not exceed the amount of the bid on the property submitted on behalf of the forfeited land commission pursuant to Section 12-51-55.

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.note: Chapter 51 was read; no section stating which liens survive a tax title was found in it.
answers.where_to_look: See Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws).

links.title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: The tax sale deed, whether to a private person, a corporation or a forfeited land commission, is prima facie evidence of a good title in the holder and that the proceedings were regular. An action to recover the land or its possession must be brought within two years from the date of sale.
answers.quote: In all cases of tax sale the deed of conveyance, whether executed to a private person, a corporation, or a forfeited land commission, is prima facie evidence of a good title in the holder, that all proceedings have been regular and that all legal requirements have been complied with. An action for the recovery of land sold pursuant to this chapter or for the recovery of the possession must not be maintained unless brought within two years from the date of sale as provided in Section 12-51-90(C).

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.note: The statute addresses legal possession only; physical removal of an occupant is not covered in chapter 51.
answers.answer: After the redemption period ends, the delinquent tax collector makes a tax title to the purchaser; delivery of the tax title to the clerk of court or register of deeds is considered putting the purchaser in possession. The law does not describe removing occupants.
answers.quote: Delivery of the tax title to the clerk of court or register of deeds is considered "putting the purchaser, or assignee, in possession".

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: The opening bid is made on behalf of the county forfeited land commission. The commission sells the lands bid in for it, on terms it decides are in the best interest of the county.
answers.quote: shall effect the sale of lands forfeited and bid in for the various forfeited land commissions of the State by the county auditors or the tax collectors of the several counties of the State in pursuance of Section 12-51-55. All lands deeded to the forfeited land commission of any county shall be held by it as assets of the county and sold to the best interest of the county.

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.office: Person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes
answers.answer: If the tax sale brings more than the taxes, assessments, penalties and costs due, the overage is applied first to any outstanding municipal tax liens; the rest belongs to the owner of record immediately before the end of the redemption period. The sums are payable ninety days after the deed is executed, and an overage neither claimed nor assigned within five years escheats to the governing body's general fund.
answers.quote: If the tax sale of an item produced more cash than the full amount due in taxes, assessments, penalties, and costs, the overage must be applied to any outstanding municipal tax liens on the property. Any remaining overage belongs to the owner of record immediately before the end of the redemption period ... These sums are payable ninety days after execution of the deed ... If neither claimed nor assigned within five years of date of public auction tax sale, the overage shall escheat to the general fund of the governing body.

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.note: No statewide due-diligence statement was found; county pages carry their own (e.g. Horry, Oconee, Georgetown).
answers.where_to_look: See Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws).

links.title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

AVAILABLE.summary: Forfeited Land Commission property: parcels bid in by the county at the tax sale, offered after the redemption period.

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: These are lands bid in for the county forfeited land commission at the delinquent tax sale. The commission holds them as assets of the county and sells them, and it may also assign its bids before the tax deed is made.
answers.quote: All lands deeded to the forfeited land commission of any county shall be held by it as assets of the county and sold to the best interest of the county. ... The forfeited land commission may assign its bids at any time before title deed being made pursuant to sale

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: For assignments of the commission's bids, the chairman may accept sealed bids for a set period; assignments not made then may be made first come, first served. The commission keeps a list of available properties at a location it chooses.
answers.quote: The chairman or his designee may accept sealed bids for assignments of the forfeited land commission bids for a designated time period. Assignments not made during this time may then be assigned on a first come, first served basis. A list of available forfeited land commission properties is to be maintained at an assigned location as determined by the county forfeited land commission.

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: An assignment of a commission bid may not be for less than the taxes, penalties and costs for which the property was sold.
answers.quote: provided the consideration to be paid for such assignments shall not be less than the amount of taxes, penalties and costs for which the property was sold.

answers.source_title: South Carolina Code of Laws, Title 12, Chapter 51 - Alternate Procedure for Collection of Property Taxes
answers.note: Applies to a buyer who takes an assignment of the forfeited land commission's bid under S.C. Code 12-59-80; the commission's own sale terms are set under 12-59-40.
answers.answer: The purchaser, or the assignee of the Forfeited Land Commission's bid, pays the actual cost of preparing the tax title plus the documentary stamps and recording fees, before the tax title is delivered for recording.
answers.quote: The successful purchaser, or assignee, is responsible for the actual cost of preparing the tax title plus documentary stamps necessary to be affixed and recording fees. The successful purchaser, or assignee, shall pay the amounts to the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes before delivery of the tax title to the clerk of court or register of deeds

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.note: The statute names no buyer form; counties publish their own bid forms (see Georgetown and Horry rows).
answers.answer: The commission's chairman or designee may accept sealed bids for assignments of the commission's bids for a set period; assignments not made then may be made first come, first served. A list of available commission properties is kept at a location the county commission chooses.
answers.quote: The chairman or his designee may accept sealed bids for assignments of the forfeited land commission bids for a designated time period. Assignments not made during this time may then be assigned on a first come, first served basis. A list of available forfeited land commission properties is to be maintained at an assigned location as determined by the county forfeited land commission.

answers.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
answers.answer: Terms are set by the commission, but any terms may not run longer than ten years for full payment and must be secured by a first real estate mortgage on the property.
answers.quote: but the terms of sale shall not in any case provide for a longer term than ten years for the full payment of the purchase price of such property and shall be secured by a first real estate mortgage upon the property sold.

answers.answer: A tax sale deed, including one made to a forfeited land commission, is prima facie evidence of good title and of regular proceedings; an action to recover the land must be brought within two years from the date of sale.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).
answers.answer: Real property seized under a tax warrant or ordered sold after foreclosure of a tax lien is sold by the officer charged with selling the property. The sale is conducted the way similar property is sold under execution, except as the Tax Code provides otherwise.
answers.quote: Real property seized under a tax warrant issued under Subchapter E , Chapter 33 , or ordered sold pursuant to foreclosure of a tax lien shall be sold by the officer charged with selling the property, unless otherwise directed by the taxing unit that requested the warrant or order of sale or by an authorized agent or attorney for that unit. The sale shall be conducted in the manner similar property is sold under execution

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).
answers.answer: An in-person sale must take place between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month (the first Wednesday if that Tuesday is January 1 or July 4). An online auction may begin at any time but must conclude at 4 p.m. on that same day.
answers.quote: must take place between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month or, if the first Tuesday of a month occurs on January 1 or July 4, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Wednesday of the month. (r-2) A sale of real property conducted by means of a public auction using online bidding and sale under Subsection (a-1) may begin at any time and must conclude at 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).
answers.answer: A tax sale must take place at the county courthouse, unless the commissioners court authorizes a public auction using online bidding and sale.
answers.quote: The commissioners court of a county by official action may authorize the officer charged with selling property under this section to conduct a public auction using online bidding and sale. … Except as provided by Subsection (a-1) and this subsection, a sale of real property under this section must take place at the county courthouse in the county in which the land is located.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer). 34.015 applies in counties of 250,000+ that have not adopted 34.011, and in smaller counties that adopt it (34.015(p)). The statement costs at most $10 and expires on the 90th day after issuance (34.015(j), (k)).
answers.answer: A commissioners court may require bidders to register with the county assessor-collector before the sale begins. The officer may not deliver a deed unless the purchaser shows an unexpired written statement issued by the county assessor-collector.
answers.quote: A commissioners court may require that, to be eligible to bid at a sale of real property under this chapter, a person must be registered as a bidder with the county assessor-collector before the sale begins. … may not execute or deliver a deed to the purchaser of the property unless the purchaser exhibits to the officer an unexpired written statement issued under this section to the person by the county assessor-collector

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).
answers.answer: The officer calculates the total amount due under the judgment: taxes, penalties and interest, any other amount awarded, court costs and the costs of the sale. If no bid sufficient to pay the lesser of that amount or the adjudged value is received, the taxing unit that requested the order of sale may end the sale.
answers.quote: The officer shall calculate the total amount due under the judgment, including all taxes, penalties, and interest, plus any other amount awarded by the judgment, court costs, and the costs of the sale. … If a bid sufficient to pay the lesser of the amount calculated under Subsection (b) or the adjudged value is not received, the taxing unit that requested the order of sale may terminate the sale.

answers.source_title: Texas Rules of Civil Procedure
answers.note: Tax Code 34.01(a) applies execution-sale procedure to tax sales.
answers.answer: Under the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure for execution sales, a bidder who fails to comply with the terms of the sale is liable to pay the plaintiff twenty percent of the value of the property plus costs, and the officer sells the property again.
answers.quote: If any person shall bid off property at any sale made by virtue of an execution, and shall fail to comply with the terms of the sale, he shall be liable to pay the plaintiff in execution twenty per cent on the value of the property thus bid off, besides costs … When the terms of the sale shall not be complied with by the bidder the levying officer shall proceed to sell the same property again on the same day, if there be sufficient time

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: The statute names no cost charged on top of the winning bid other than the statement fee; county pages add deed recording fees and post-judgment taxes (see county rows).
answers.answer: The Tax Code counts the costs of sale - advertising, an auctioneer's commission and fees, and anticipated deed recording fees - inside the total amount due that the officer calculates for the sale. Separately, the county assessor-collector may charge a fee of up to $10 for each written statement a purchaser requests to show that no delinquent taxes are owed.
answers.quote: The costs of a sale include the costs of advertising, an auctioneer's commission and fees, and deed recording fees anticipated to be paid in connection with the sale of the property. ... To cover the costs associated with the issuance of statements under Subsection (c), a county assessor-collector may charge the person requesting a statement a fee not to exceed $10 for each statement requested.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).
answers.answer: The deed vests good and perfect title in the purchaser to the defendant's interest in the property, including the right to use and possess it, subject to the defendant's right of redemption (and the recorded covenants and easements listed in the statute). It may be impeached only for fraud.
answers.quote: The deed vests good and perfect title in the purchaser or the purchaser's assigns to the interest owned by the defendant in the property subject to the foreclosure, including the defendant's right to the use and possession of the property, subject only to the defendant's right of redemption … The deed may be impeached only for fraud.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer). The two-year rule in 34.21(a) applies to a residence homestead, land designated for agricultural use, or a mineral interest; 34.21(e) gives the 180-day period (premium not over 25 percent) for all other property.
answers.answer: Yes. For a residence homestead or land designated for agricultural use, the owner may redeem on or before the second anniversary of the date the purchaser's deed is filed, paying the amount bid and other statutory amounts plus a 25% premium in the first year or 50% in the second. For other property the right must be exercised within 180 days after the deed is filed.
answers.quote: may redeem the property on or before the second anniversary of the date on which the purchaser's deed is filed for record by paying the purchaser the amount the purchaser bid for the property … plus a redemption premium of 25 percent of the aggregate total if the property is redeemed during the first year of the redemption period or 50 percent … may be exercised not later than the 180th day following the date on which the purchaser's or taxing unit's deed is filed for record

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer). First quoted part from 34.01(n); second from 34.01(q)(1). The deed also remains subject to the defendant's right of redemption.
answers.answer: A sale to a purchaser other than a taxing unit extinguishes each lien securing the delinquent taxes, penalties and interest included in the judgment. Title remains subject to restrictive covenants recorded before January 1 of the year the tax lien arose, a recorded lien under such a covenant not extinguished in the judgment, and valid easements of record (34.01(n)).
answers.quote: a recorded restrictive covenant running with the land that was recorded before January 1 of the year in which the tax lien on the property arose, a recorded lien that arose under that restrictive covenant that was not extinguished in the judgment foreclosing the tax lien, and each valid easement of record … extinguishes each lien securing payment of the delinquent taxes, penalties, and interest against that property and included in the judgment

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: The Tax Code does not address title insurance. 34.08(b) also bars a challenge after the Section 33.54 period against a subsequent purchaser for value, who may presume the sale valid.
answers.answer: The statute says the officer's deed may be impeached only for fraud. A person may not bring an action challenging the validity of the tax sale unless the person deposits into the court registry the delinquent taxes, penalties and interest specified in the judgment plus all costs of the sale, or files an affidavit of inability to pay under Rule 145.
answers.quote: The deed may be impeached only for fraud. ... A person may not commence an action that challenges the validity of a tax sale under this chapter unless the person: (1) deposits into the registry of the court an amount equal to the amount of the delinquent taxes, penalties, and interest specified in the judgment of foreclosure obtained against the property plus all costs of the tax sale; or (2) files an affidavit of inability to pay under Rule 145, Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Chapter 34 does not describe removing occupants; that is outside this statute text.
answers.answer: The statute says the right of redemption does not give the former owner the right to use or possess the property, or to receive rents, income or other benefits from it, while the right of redemption exists.
answers.quote: (h) The right of redemption does not grant or reserve in the former owner of the real property the right to the use or possession of the property, or to receive rents, income, or other benefits from the property while the right of redemption exists.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).
answers.answer: If no sufficient bid is received and the taxing unit does not end the sale, the officer bids the property off to the taxing unit that requested the order of sale, for the lesser of the judgment amount or the market value in the judgment. That taxing unit takes title for itself and the other taxing units in the suit.
answers.quote: the officer making the sale shall bid the property off to the taxing unit that requested the order of sale … for the aggregate amount of the judgment against the property or for the market value of the property as specified in the judgment, whichever is less. … The taxing unit to which the property is bid off takes title to the property for the use and benefit of itself and all other taxing units that established tax liens in the suit.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.office: Clerk of the court that ordered the sale
answers.note: 34.04(c) lists the priority: a purchaser whose sale was voided, later taxes, other lienholders, unsatisfied judgment amounts, then former owners.
answers.answer: The officer pays any excess proceeds to the clerk of the court that issued the warrant or order of sale. The clerk keeps them for two years after the sale unless the court orders otherwise; a claim must be filed by petition in the court before the second anniversary of the sale, and the court orders the proceeds paid by a set order of priorities.

AVAILABLE.summary: Property struck off to a taxing unit after no sufficient bid, which the unit may later resell under its own process.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).
answers.answer: These are properties sold to a taxing unit at a tax sale. Such a taxing unit may sell the property at any time by public or private sale, subject to any right of redemption of the former owner; the redemption period begins when the deed to the taxing unit is filed for record.
answers.quote: If property is sold to a taxing unit that is a party to the judgment, the taxing unit may sell the property at any time by public or private sale. … The sale is subject to any right of redemption of the former owner. The redemption period begins on the date the deed to the taxing unit is filed for record.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer). How a particular taxing unit takes offers is set locally (see county rows).
answers.answer: The taxing unit that bought the property may ask the sheriff or a constable to sell it at a public sale, or may instead sell it at a private sale.
answers.quote: The taxing unit purchasing the property by resolution of its governing body may request the sheriff or a constable to sell the property at a public sale. … In lieu of a sale pursuant to Subsections (c) and (d) of this section, the taxing unit that purchased the property may sell the property at a private sale.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).
answers.answer: A public resale requested by the taxing unit may be for any amount. A private sale under 34.05(h) may not be for less than the lesser of the market value in the judgment or the total judgments against the property.
answers.quote: Property sold pursuant to Subsections (c) and (d) of this section may be sold for any amount. … Property sold under this subsection may not be sold for an amount that is less than the lesser of: (1) the market value specified in the judgment of foreclosure; or (2) the total amount of the judgments against the property.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer). The statute states this for 34.05(j) sales only; other resale costs are set locally (see county rows).
answers.answer: For a private sale at or above market value under 34.05(j), the conveyance is subject to the purchaser's obligation to pay the prorated taxes for the current year.
answers.quote: The conveyance is subject to any remaining right of redemption at the time of the sale and to the purchaser's obligation to pay the prorated taxes for the current year as provided by Section 26.10 .

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).
answers.answer: The taxing unit may sell the property at any time. If it has not sold the property within six months after the owner's right of redemption ends, any taxing unit entitled to the proceeds may ask the sheriff or a constable in writing to sell it at a public sale.
answers.quote: If the purchasing taxing unit has not sold the property within six months after the date on which the owner's right of redemption terminates, any taxing unit that is entitled to receive proceeds of the sale by resolution of its governing body may request the sheriff or a constable in writing to sell the property at a public sale.

answers.source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
answers.note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server. Subsection (k) also keeps the prorated current-year tax with the purchaser.
answers.answer: A resale by a taxing unit is subject to any remaining right of redemption of the former owner. A private sale at or above market value under Subsection (j) discharges and extinguishes all liens foreclosed by the judgment.
answers.quote: The sale is subject to any right of redemption of the former owner. ... The conveyance shall be made subject to any remaining right of redemption at the time of the sale. ... A sale under Subsection (j) discharges and extinguishes all liens foreclosed by the judgment

answers.answer: An action attacking the validity of a resale of property by a taxing unit may not be instituted after the expiration of one year after the date of the resale.
answers.quote: An action attacking the validity of a resale of property pursuant to this section may not be instituted after the expiration of one year after the date of the resale.

answers.note: Travis County Tax Office FAQ. Denton County's Sheriff's Sale Rules say the same: 'There is no Tax Lien Certificate Sale in Texas.' (The source says this is not done here.)
answers.answer: Texas does not sell tax lien certificates. The tax office sells no tax liens; the property itself is sold at the monthly tax foreclosure sale.
answers.quote: The tax office does not sell tax liens. Texas law allows the public to purchase properties from the county at a monthly tax foreclosure sale. The states sells the deed to the property. Note: The state does not sell tax lien certificates where a buyer becomes the lienholder for the back taxes.

answers.answer: Tax sales begin at 10:00 a.m. on the first Tuesday of the month, but are not conducted every month in Bell County - there are usually 4 to 5 tax sales a year.
answers.quote: Tax sales begin at 10:00 a.m. on the first Tuesday of the month and are held at the Bell County Clerk’s Alcove outside to the east of the main entrance of the Bell County Justice Complex, 1201 Huey Drive, in Belton. ... Tax Sales are not conducted every month in Bell County. There are usually 4 to 5 tax sales a year.

answers.source_title: Property Tax Sales - Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.office: Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.answer: In person only: bidders must be present at the sale, held at the Bell County Clerk's Alcove outside to the east of the main entrance of the Bell County Justice Complex, 1201 Huey Drive, in Belton; bids are not accepted by mail, phone or internet.
answers.quote: Bidders must be present at the tax sale. Bids will not be accepted via mail, phone or internet. ... are held at the Bell County Clerk’s Alcove outside to the east of the main entrance of the Bell County Justice Complex, 1201 Huey Drive, in Belton.

answers.source_title: Property Tax Sales - Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.office: Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.note: A person bidding for a business entity must present a Power of Attorney or other authorization.
answers.answer: All bidders register with the person conducting the sale before it begins; registration starts at approximately 9:45 a.m. on the day of the sale and requires a valid driver's license or identification card issued by a State Agency or the United States Government.
answers.quote: All bidders must register to bid prior to the sale with the person conducting the sale. If you do not register prior to the beginning of the sale, you may not bid. Registration will begin at approximately 9:45 a.m. the day of the sale ... Bidders must present a valid driver’s license or identification card issued by a State Agency or the United States Government at the time of registration.

answers.source_title: Property Tax Sales - Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.note: A bidder who does not pay faces collection under Rule 652 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure, per the page.
answers.answer: The full purchase price is paid by cashier's check payable to the Bell County District Clerk, at the District Clerk's Office at the Justice Complex between 1:00 and 3:00 pm on the day of the sale; personal checks are not accepted.
answers.quote: Bidders must have the funds readily accessible with which to pay the purchase price in full. ... The cashier’s check should be made payable to the Bell County District Clerk. ... Personal checks will not be accepted ... The Bell County District Clerk’s Office will accept your payment between 1:00 and 3:00 pm on the day of the sale.

answers.source_title: Property Tax Sales - Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.office: Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.answer: Purchasers pay all taxes that became or will become delinquent after the date of judgment, the deed recording fee at the conclusion of the sale (two pages is $14.00), and a $10.00 fee for the document showing no delinquent taxes are owed.
answers.quote: The minimum bid includes all taxes which were delinquent at the date of Judgment. Purchasers will be required to pay all taxes which became or will become delinquent subsequent to the date of Judgment. ... You will be required to pay for the deed recording fee at the conclusion of the tax sale. Most deeds are two pages and the fee for two pages is $14.00. ... There is a $10.00 fee for this document which will be collected at the conclusion of the sale.

answers.source_title: Property Tax Sales - Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.office: Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.answer: Yes. The redemption period begins when the purchaser's deed is recorded: 2 years for homestead property and land designated for agricultural use, 180 days for all other property. The redemption price is the purchase amount, deed recording fee, taxes paid and costs, plus a premium of 25 percent in the first year or 50 percent in the second.
answers.quote: The redemption period begins on the date that the purchaser’s deed is recorded in the County Clerk’s office. The redemption period for homestead property and land designated for agricultural use is 2 years. ... The redemption period for all other property is 180 days. ... purchase amount, deed recording fee, taxes paid by the purchaser after the tax sale, and costs expended on the property, plus a redemption premium of 25 percent of the aggregate total during the first year or 50 percent of the aggregate total during the second year.

answers.source_title: Property Tax Sales - Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.office: Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.answer: The sale should extinguish the ownership interests and recorded liens of everyone named as a defendant in the judgment, including IRS tax liens; the purchaser takes title subject to the interest or lien of any party not named as a defendant, and the property may be subject to City or Property Owners Association liens for demolition, mowing or maintenance fees.
answers.quote: The tax sale should extinguish the record ownership interest of all persons and the recorded liens of all persons who were named as defendants in the judgment on which the tax sale is based, including any tax liens filed by the Internal Revenue Service. If a party who has an ownership interest or holds a lien on the property was NOT named as a defendant in the judgment, the purchaser at the tax sale will take title to the property subject to the interest or lien of that party. ... Property purchased at the tax sale may be subject to liens for demolition, mowing, or maintenance fees

answers.source_title: Property Tax Sales - Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.office: Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.answer: Purchasers receive an ordinary Sheriff's Deed without warranty, expressed or implied; title is not guaranteed and a policy of title insurance may be difficult to obtain.
answers.quote: Purchasers of property at the tax sale will receive an ordinary type of Sheriff’s Deed which is without warranty, either expressed or implied. Title to property sold at the tax sale is NOT guaranteed. A policy of title insurance on the property purchased at the tax sale may be difficult to obtain.

answers.source_title: Property Tax Sales - Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.office: Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.answer: Neither the Tax Appraisal District nor the Bell County Sheriff's Department puts the purchaser in possession at the sale; purchasers have the right to a Writ of Possession on the 20th day after the deed is filed of record, and the page points to Section 33.51 of the Tax Code for the procedure for occupied property.
answers.quote: neither the Tax Appraisal District of Bell County nor the Bell County Sheriff’s Department will put you in possession of the property at the time of the tax sale. Purchasers have the right to a Writ of Possession on the 20 th day following the date on which the purchaser’s deed is filed of record with the County Clerk. See Section 33.51 of the Tax Code for the procedures for gaining possession of occupied property.

answers.source_title: Property Tax Sales - Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.office: Tax Appraisal District of Bell County
answers.answer: The Appraisal District tells bidders to view the property from public streets or roadways before the sale and satisfy themselves about its location and condition; it cannot give permission to enter the property. All property is sold by legal description, "AS IS" with all faults, and the approximate address on the bid sheet may not be accurate.
answers.quote: Prior to the sale, bidders should view the property and satisfy themselves as to the location and condition of the property. After the sale is too late. ... cannot give you permission to go onto or access the property prior to the sale. Do not trespass. You should view the property from public streets or roadways. All property is sold by legal description. Property is sold “AS IS” with all faults. ... Any “approximate property address” reflected on the bid sheet is the address on the tax records and may not be accurate.

answers.source_title: Bexar County Tax Foreclosure Struck Off Properties General Information
answers.answer: The buyer signs a Purchase Agreement listing all costs; the file then goes to Commissioners Court for formal approval and a Court Order authorizing the sale.

answers.source_title: Bexar County Tax Foreclosure Struck Off Properties General Information
answers.answer: After Commissioners Court approval the buyer first pays the interim taxes to the Tax Assessor/Collector, then the struck-off amount (and any code compliance liens) by cashier's check payable to the Bexar County Sheriff, and last the deed recording fee payable to the County Clerk.
answers.quote: After formal approval by the Commissioner's Court, the purchaser will first make payment to Bexar County Tax Assessor/Collector's office, for the interim taxes due. … the next collection of payment is for the struck off amount and that amount needed to satisfy the code compliance liens if any, in the form of a cashier's check made payable to Bexar County Sheriff. The last payment is for the recording fee

answers.source_title: Sheriff Sale | Randall County, TX
answers.answer: The Randall County Tax Office says there are two Sheriff Sales a year, in April and August, on the first Tuesday of the month, and you must register to bid.
answers.quote: We have two Sheriff Sales a year. One in April and one in August. They are the first Tuesday of the month. You do have to register in order to bid.

answers.source_title: Bidder Registration Procedures (Randall County Tax Assessor-Collector)
answers.answer: Randall County requires a valid government-issued photo ID, a signed statement that you have no delinquent taxes on property in Randall County, and a registration renewed each year (accepted February 1 to August 1).
answers.quote: You must have a valid, government issued, photo ID. ... You CANNOT have delinquent taxes due on any property owned in Randall County and you must sign a statement attesting to that fact on your Bidder Registration application. ... You must renew your registration each year. Registrations will be accepted between February 1 and August 1.

answers.source_title: Bidder Registration Procedures (Randall County Tax Assessor-Collector)

answers.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions
answers.note: Tax Assessor-Collector phone 817-884-1186 is on the same page.
answers.answer: Tarrant County Constable Precinct 3 conducts all delinquent tax sales in Tarrant County; its phone is 817-581-3610 Option 2.
answers.quote: Constable Darrell Huffman, Tarrant County Precinct 3 Constable, is charged with the responsibility of conducting all Delinquent Tax Sales in Tarrant County. These sales are conducted by a deputy constable based in the Southlake Town Square. The phone number is 817-581-3610 Option 2.

answers.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions
answers.answer: Tarrant County tax sales are held on the first Tuesday of each month on the 1895 Courthouse steps between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m.; tax sales begin at 10 a.m.
answers.quote: Pursuant to Texas law, all sales are held on the first Tuesday of each month. … All property sales are held on the 1895 Courthouse steps between the hours of 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Tax sales begin at 10 a.m..

answers.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions
answers.answer: In person only: bidders must be present at the sale to bid.
answers.quote: No, you must be present at the sale, in person, to bid.

answers.source_title: Delinquent Tax Sales
answers.answer: Bidders must register before 10 a.m.; registrations are not accepted after the sale has begun.
answers.quote: Bidders MUST register prior to 10 a.m. We will no longer accept registrations after the sale has begun.

answers.source_title: Delinquent Tax Sales
answers.answer: Payment is accepted only as cashier's checks and money orders in the exact amount; purchasers have up to one hour after the sale to bring certified funds.
answers.quote: Payments are only accepted in these forms: cashier checks and money orders. … Purchasers have up to one hour after the sale to bring in certified funds in the exact amount.

answers.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions
answers.note: Tax Assessor-Collector phone 817-884-1186 is on the same page.
answers.answer: Tarrant County Constable Precinct 3 conducts all delinquent tax sales in Tarrant County; its phone is 817-581-3610 Option 2.
answers.quote: Constable Darrell Huffman, Tarrant County Precinct 3 Constable, is charged with the responsibility of conducting all Delinquent Tax Sales in Tarrant County. These sales are conducted by a deputy constable based in the Southlake Town Square. The phone number is 817-581-3610 Option 2.

answers.source_title: Tarrant County Constable Precinct 3 - Frequently Asked Questions
answers.answer: Properties struck off at the auction are bid on by the taxing entities, and the deeds are issued in the name of the taxing entity, which then becomes the owner.
answers.quote: The properties that are struck off at the auction are actually bid on by the taxing entities. The deeds are issued to the property in the name of the taxing entity. The taxing entity then becomes the owner of that property and they can do with the property what they wish.

answers.source_title: City of Fort Worth Tax Foreclosed Property Inventory - Frequently Asked Questions
answers.office: City of Fort Worth Property Management
answers.note: The FAQ (revised May 2016) says properties struck off at the Tarrant County sale are transferred to the city where they lie and that Fort Worth serves as trustee for all Tarrant County taxing entities.
answers.answer: When the City of Fort Worth has tax-foreclosed properties for sale it posts a list and bid forms on its website and advertises in the Fort Worth Star Telegram with a minimum bid amount and the sale date. Properties may also be sold directly to an interested buyer who submits a written request with confirmation of sufficient funds to pay the entire cash amount.
answers.quote: When the City has tax foreclosed properties for sale, a list will be posted on the City’s website: www.fortworthtexas.gov/propertymanagement/realproperty. Bid forms will also be posted on the website. Properties may also be sold directly to interested buyer(s). The advertisement will also be available in the Fort Worth Star Telegram with a minimum bid amount and the sale date. ... The interested buyer must submit a written request and include confirmation that they have sufficient funds to pay the entire cash amount due prior to the conveyance of the property.

answers.source_title: City of Fort Worth Tax Foreclosed Property Inventory - Frequently Asked Questions
answers.office: City of Fort Worth Property Management
answers.answer: Purchase prices are not listed on the inventory list; when properties are identified for sealed bid, minimum bid amounts are determined and posted.
answers.quote: Purchase prices are not listed on the inventory list. When properties are identified for sealed bid, minimum bid amounts are determined and posted.

answers.source_title: City of Fort Worth Tax Foreclosed Property Inventory - Frequently Asked Questions
answers.office: City of Fort Worth Property Management
answers.answer: The City may charge up to $1,600 in administrative fees, included in the balance letter sent to the buyer; the new owner is responsible for taxes from the date the Tax Resale Deed is transferred into their name.
answers.quote: The City may charge up to $1,600 for administrative fees. This amount is included in the balance letter sent to the buyer. ... As the new owner of the property, you will be responsible for the taxes owed starting on the date the Tax Resale Deed is transferred into your name.

answers.source_title: City of Fort Worth Tax Foreclosed Property Inventory - Frequently Asked Questions
answers.office: City of Fort Worth Property Management
answers.answer: After City Council approves the sale, staff send a letter with the amount due; the balance is paid in full within 15 days of the letter's date, by certified bank check or cashier's check only.
answers.quote: After the sale of the property is approved by City Council, staff will send you a letter to give you the amount due. The balance must be paid in full within 15 days from the date of the letter. ... All payments must be in the form of a certified bank check or a cashier’s check - no exceptions.

answers.source_title: City of Fort Worth Tax Foreclosed Property Inventory - Frequently Asked Questions
answers.office: City of Fort Worth Property Management
answers.answer: The City releases labor, weed, demolition, board-up and mowing liens before the property is transferred; other liens cannot be released by the City.
answers.quote: The City will release labor, weed, demolition, board-up and mowing liens before the property is transferred to the new owner. Please note that other liens cannot be released by the City and the buyer is urged to research the chain of title through a title company of their choice.

answers.source_title: City of Fort Worth Tax Foreclosed Property Inventory - Frequently Asked Questions
answers.office: City of Fort Worth Property Management
answers.answer: No: properties are sold "as is" and the City is unable to provide access to the tax-foreclosed properties.
answers.quote: Properties are sold “as is” and the City is unable to provide access to the tax-foreclosed properties.

answers.source_title: City of Fort Worth Tax Foreclosed Property Inventory - Frequently Asked Questions
answers.office: City of Fort Worth Property Management
answers.answer: The City says it is the bidder's responsibility to research the property title before placing a bid - it does not release IRS or mechanic's liens - and urges buyers to research the chain of title through a title company of their choice.
answers.quote: The City is not responsible for releasing or dismissing these types of liens; it is the bidder’s responsibility to research the property title before placing a bid. ... the buyer is urged to research the chain of title through a title company of their choice.
