answers.source_title: Tax Deed Details | Dane County Treasurer Office
answers.answer: By sealed bid, using the "Bid Form" button next to each parcel on the Tax Deed Auction page; bids are opened at the Treasurer's Office.
answers.quote: Auctions are conducted through a sealed bid. The Bid Due date is the day before the Bid Opening. ... Bids can be accepted using the "Bid Form" button next to the specific parcel.

answers.source_title: Tax Deed Details | Dane County Treasurer Office
answers.answer: No registration is required to submit a bid.
answers.quote: No registration required to submit a bid.

answers.source_title: Tax Deed Details | Dane County Treasurer Office
answers.answer: Yes: an earnest deposit of 10% of the bid, in cash or cashier's check, must be in the sealed envelope with each bid form.
answers.quote: All payments must be in the form of cash or cashiers check. Auction Bidder: Earnest Deposit (10% of the bid) must accompany each completed corresponding bid form within the sealed envelope

answers.source_title: Tax Deeded Land Sales - Access Dane
answers.answer: The sale notice lists each parcel's appraised value and the date it becomes available; the treasurer sells each parcel to the highest bidder whose unconditional bid equals or exceeds the advertised appraised value.
answers.quote: The treasurer will publish a notice for the sale of tax-deeded lands, describing each parcel for sale, its appraised value, and the date on and after which the parcel will be available for purchase. ... the treasurer shall sell each parcel to the highest bidder whose unconditional bid is equal to or exceeds the advertised appraised value of the parcel.

answers.source_title: Tax Deed Details | Dane County Treasurer Office
answers.answer: The balance of the bid must reach the Treasurer's Office within ten days of receiving the award letter, in cash or cashier's check. On default the 10% earnest money is kept and the next bidder is offered the parcel.
answers.quote: Successful Bidder: Balance of bid must be received by the Dane County Treasurer's Office within ten (10) days of receiving the bid award notification letter. IMPORTANT: No payment arrangements, personal or business checks, credit or debit card transactions, ACH, or wire payments. ... The 10% earnest money will be kept by Dane County.

answers.source_title: Tax Deed Details | Dane County Treasurer Office
answers.answer: Depending on when the property is bought, the purchaser may have to pay the most recent tax year's taxes and specials to the municipality (for example, December - January purchases, and Madison parcels).
answers.quote: December - January: Successful Purchaser will pay in-full the most recent taxes and any associated specials to the municipality (city/village/town). ... Madison parcels: Successful Purchaser will pay in-full the most recent taxes and any associated specials, interest, and penalty to Madison

answers.answer: A parcel not sold by bid on the first sale date may be sold by the treasurer at any time afterwards to anyone offering at or above the appraised value; offers go to the Treasurer's Office in writing, no earlier than the day after the bid opening.

answers.answer: After a sale the county returns any net proceeds to the former owner, on or about the time of the next auction (typically October and April); unclaimed net proceeds go into the Unclaimed Funds process.
answers.quote: The county will return any net proceeds to the former owner upon sale. Any net proceeds would be returned on or about the timing of the subsequent auction after sale (typically October & April). If net proceeds go unclaimed, the net proceeds will be transferred into the Unclaimed Funds process.

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: The county treasurer sells real property for delinquent taxes. The person who offers to pay the taxes, interest, penalties and costs is the purchaser and receives a certificate of purchase from the treasurer.
answers.quote: Any person who offers to pay the amount of taxes, interest, penalties and costs including charges provided by paragraph (ix) of this subsection due on any real property is considered the purchaser thereof. ... the county treasurer upon payment of the fee provided by subparagraph (ix)(B) of this subsection shall make out, sign and deliver a certificate of purchase to the purchaser

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: The sale is advertised once a week for three weeks in a legal newspaper, with the first publication at least four weeks before the sale and before the first week in September. Sales run between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Sundays excluded, and may be adjourned day to day until all lands are sold.
answers.quote: he shall advertise notice of all sales of real property by publication thereof, once a week for three (3) weeks in a legal newspaper in the county, the first publication to be at least four (4) weeks prior to the day of sale and prior to the first week in September. ... between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Sundays excluded, and may be adjourned from day-to-day until all lands are sold

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: Sales of real property are held at the county courthouse or county building.
answers.quote: Sales of real property shall be held at the county courthouse or county building between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Sundays excluded

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: The amount is the taxes, interest, penalties and costs due on the property, including the statutory charges.
answers.quote: Any person who offers to pay the amount of taxes, interest, penalties and costs including charges provided by paragraph (ix) of this subsection due on any real property is considered the purchaser thereof.

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: The purchaser must pay the county treasurer all amounts due immediately; otherwise the property is offered again and the original purchaser is disqualified.
answers.quote: The purchaser shall immediately pay the county treasurer all amounts due on the real property in the absence of which the real property shall again be offered for sale and the original purchaser disqualified.

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: The treasurer collects up to $20.00 for advertising a real property sale and up to $20.00 for issuing a certificate of purchase.
answers.quote: not to exceed twenty dollars ($20.00) for advertising in the case of sale of real property to collect delinquent taxes; (B) Not to exceed twenty dollars ($20.00) for issuing a certificate of purchase

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: The buyer first receives a certificate of purchase. The treasurer issues a tax deed for unredeemed property 4 to 6 years after the sale on proper application; the tax deed is prima facie evidence of title, subject to special assessments for local or public improvements.
answers.quote: The county treasurer shall accept applications and issue tax deeds for unredeemed real property subject to a certificate of purchase not less than four (4) nor more than six (6) years from the date of the original sale ... the deed is prima facie evidence of title to the property described subject to special assessments for local or public improvements.

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: Yes. The legal owner may redeem after the sale until a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted by the county treasurer.
answers.quote: Real property sold for delinquent taxes may be redeemed by the legal owner after the date of sale but before a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted by the county treasurer pursuant to W.S. 39-13-108(e)(v)(A)

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: The certificate holder takes subject to special assessments for local or public improvements. The certificate or tax deed holder's lien is superior to all other liens except those created by junior tax sales or payment of subsequent taxes by another person.
answers.quote: The holder of the certificate of purchase takes subject to any special assessments for local or public improvements. ... The lien is superior to all other liens except those created by junior tax sales or payment of subsequent taxes by another person.

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.answer: A tax deed or county commissioner's deed is prima facie evidence of title to the property, subject to special assessments for local or public improvements. Anyone seeking to invalidate that title carries the burden of proof.
answers.quote: the deed is prima facie evidence of title to the property described subject to special assessments for local or public improvements. The burden of proof shall be upon any party seeking to invalidate title conveyed by a tax or county commissioner's deed in any action in any court in Wyoming

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: The statute does not describe removing an occupant.
answers.answer: Before applying for a tax deed, the certificate holder must show that at least three (3) months earlier a notice was served on each person in actual possession or occupancy of the property. A tax deed grantee and successors in title are entitled to possession of the property.
answers.quote: That at least three (3) months prior to the application a written or printed notice was served on each person in actual possession or occupancy of the real property ... Any grantee of a tax deed or county commissioner's deed pursuant to paragraph (iv) or (v) of this subsection, and successors in title are entitled to possession of the real property conveyed by the deed

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: Property that cannot be sold for the taxes, interest, penalties and costs is bid in for the county. The county commissioners may sell and assign those certificates at public or private sale at any time; after four years the treasurer issues a tax deed to the county for unredeemed certificates it holds.
answers.quote: Any real property which cannot be sold for the amount of taxes, interest, penalties and costs shall be bid in for the county by the county treasurer. ... The county commissioners of any county may sell and assign any certificate of purchase for real property bid in for the county ... at public or private sale at any time.

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: The legal owner may redeem after the sale until a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted; the treasurer accepts tax deed applications no less than four years after the sale.
answers.quote: may be redeemed by the legal owner after the date of sale but before a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted by the county treasurer ... accept applications and issue tax deeds for unredeemed real property subject to a certificate of purchase not less than four (4) nor more than six (6) years from the date of the original sale

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
answers.answer: The holder applies to the treasurer, returns the certificate of purchase, pays the fees and proves the required notice was given - including a notice served at least three (3) months before the application on each person in possession and on the person in whose name the property was taxed.
answers.quote: upon proper application, return of the certificate of purchase, payment of fees and proof of compliance with the notice requirements of this section ... That at least three (3) months prior to the application a written or printed notice was served on each person in actual possession or occupancy of the real property and the person in whose name the property was taxed

answers.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
answers.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14). The statute does not use the word 'expire'; these are its time limits.
answers.answer: The treasurer accepts tax deed applications no more than six years after the original sale. An action to enforce the certificate holder's lien may be started no earlier than four and no later than ten years after the sale.
answers.quote: not less than four (4) nor more than six (6) years from the date of the original sale for taxes ... No action provided by this section may be commenced less than four (4) years nor more than ten (10) years from the date of the original tax sale.

answers.source_title: Treasurer | Albany County, WY
answers.answer: The Albany County Treasurer's office, 525 E Grand Avenue Suite 205, Laramie WY 82070, is open Monday - Friday 9:00 a.m. through 5:00 p.m.
answers.quote: Our office is open Monday – Friday 9:00 a.m. through 5:00 p.m. ... 525 E Grand Avenue Suite 205 Laramie WY 82070

answers.source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Albany County, WY
answers.answer: The 2027 tax sale date is August 13, 2027, at the Albany County Fairgrounds Activity Building.
answers.quote: 2027 Tax Sale Date: ... August 13, 2027 ... Held at the Albany County Fairgrounds, in the east side of the Activity Building located at:

answers.source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Albany County, WY
answers.answer: Buyers attend in person: buyer numbers are drawn at random in rounds, and a buyer whose number is drawn may purchase one property by calling out its property number.
answers.quote: 1st Round: random drawing of buyer numbers will be used. When your number is drawn, you have the opportunity to purchase one piece of property by calling out the ... Continuing Rounds: will be the same as the 1st round.

answers.source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Albany County, WY
answers.answer: The name on the registration form must match the name used for payment. Buyers must be present and 18 years of age, only one buyer per taxpayer ID number is allowed, and each buyer gets one number at registration.
answers.quote: The name on the registration form must be the same name under which the payment will be made ... Tax buyers must be present to participate. Parents, relatives and friends cannot purchase in the name of another individual ... Buyers must be 18 years of age to participate ... Each buyer will be assigned a number at registration. Only one number per buyer will be allowed

answers.source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Albany County, WY
answers.answer: All purchases must be paid for by 5 pm, August 13, 2027, by cash, check, money order, or VISA, Master Card and bank debit cards; card transactions carry a 2.49% convenience fee with a minimum fee of $1.50 (American Express 3.5% + $1.50).
answers.quote: All purchases must be paid for by 5 ... August 13, 2027. ... Accepted methods include only: ... Money order ... VISA, Master Card, and bank debit cards ... All credit and debit card transactions are subject to a 2.49% convenience fee with a minimum fee of $1.50 except American Express which is subject to 3.5% + $1.50 convenience fee

answers.source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Albany County, WY
answers.answer: The county warns that a tax deed may be invalidated for many reasons and that purchasers take certificates of purchase with full knowledge of these inherent problems.
answers.quote: There is a growing concern about the validity of tax deeds around the country. A tax deed may be invalidated for many reasons. We take every precaution that the deeds issued are correct. Tax sale purchasers take certificates of purchase subject to these provisions and with full knowledge of these inherent problems.

answers.source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Albany County, WY
answers.answer: A certificate holder may not remove or add anything to the property and may not contact the property owner; all correspondence goes through the Albany County Treasurer.
answers.quote: You as a certificate holder may not remove or add anything to the property. You may not contact the property owner; all correspondence will go through the Albany County Treasurer

answers.source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Albany County, WY
answers.answer: A Certificate of Purchase is $20, the reassignment fee is $25 and issuance of a Treasurer's Deed is $25.
answers.quote: Certificate of Purchase is $20 ... Reassignment fee if $25 ... Issuance of a Treasurer’s Deed is $25

answers.source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Albany County, WY
answers.answer: Bankruptcy will stop the collection of interest, and if the holder does not pay later taxes the property is sold again at the next regular tax sale as if no previous sale had been made.
answers.quote: Bankruptcy will stop the collection of interest ... When a Certificate has been purchased and the holder does not pay subsequent taxes, the property shall be advertised with all other delinquent taxes and sold at the next regular tax sale as if no previous sale had been made.
